GRP_BM.name: BM_MODEL
GRP_BM.explanation: Report the model of the instrument (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station). Use the LIST to identify the option that includes the instrument. The updated list is available online at www.icos-etc.eu/documents/templates and in the Online Tool and added to the template yearly. If your sensor is not in the list please contact the ICOS ETC.

GRP_BM.name: BM_SN
GRP_BM.description: Serial number or other unique text string used to identify this instrument
GRP_BM.explanation: Report the serial number of the instrument (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station)

GRP_BM.name: BM_TYPE
GRP_BM.description: Operations, maintenance or event happening at the sensor
GRP_BM.explanation:
Report the type of operation, maintenance or event performed/happened to the instrument using the LIST options. This variable is linked to the others in the group. The aim of the variable when reporting a maintenance, a calibration or a disturbance is only to identify the period where measurements can be affected.
In case of Field calibration, the new parameters or equation should be submitted using the INST_CALIB_FUNCTION variable.
In case of Firmware update the new firmware code should be submitted using the INST_FIRMWARE variable.
For changes in the logger, file, sampling frequency or variable name use either "Installation" (when installed) or "Variable map".

choices.description: Disturbance to the instrument
Calibration of an instrument in the field
Check of calibration of an instrument in the field
Cleaning an instrument or its parts
Firmware update
Installation of the instrument in the field
General maintenance of instrument
Replacement of parts of instruments
Connection failure that didn't allow data transmission (but data are collected)
Removal of an instrument from the station
Mapping of the instrument to one variable
Use this to report a general comment not fitting with the other options

GRP_BM.name: BM_VARIABLE_H_V_R
GRP_BM.description: Variable code suffixed by positional indices
GRP_BM.explanation:
Report here the measured variable that is linked to the instrument model and serial number reported in BM_MODEL and BM_SN. The entry must  be composed by the measured variable code and suffixes indicating the position e.g. TS_1_1_1 (see data submission instructions).
This variable can be reported when BM_TYPE is either "Installation" or "Variable Map" and in this case also the variables BM_SAMPLING_INT, BM_LOGGER and BM_FILE must be filled.
It can be reported also when BM_TYPE is "Maintenance", "Disturbances", "Field Calibration", "Field Calibration Check", "Field Cleaning", "Firmware Update" and "Part Substitution", but only if the activity affects one of the multiple variables measured by the sensor (to indicate the variable affected).
Report only the physical unit variable code, the instrument unit version will be automatically associated (e.g. don't report TS_IU_1_1_1 but just TS_1_1_1). Report only WTD (WCP will be associated automatically). Report only G (G_SF and G_ISCAL will be associated automatically). LW_T_BODY and SW_T_BODY don't need to be reported (will be associated to the LW or SW with the same indexes). Backup Meteo sensors are treated like the other meteo sensors (just different H_V_R)

GRP_BM.name: BM_HEIGHT
GRP_BM.explanation: Use as reference level the organic-mineral horizons boundary or the surface when not possible to identify (see Instruction on Soil Meteo). This variable can be reported only (and is mandatory) with BM_TYPE "Installation" and together with BM_EASTWARD_DIST and BM_NORTHWARD_DIST

GRP_BM.name: BM_EASTWARD_DIST
GRP_BM.description: Distance E-W from the site reference point. West of the reference point is negative.
GRP_BM.explanation: Measure the east-west distance from the site reference point (see Site Description Instruction). Use magnetic north as a reference. This variable can be reported only  (and is mandatory) with BM_TYPE "Installation" and together with BM_NORTHREF, BM_NORTHWARD_DIST and BM_HEIGHT

GRP_BM.name: BM_NORTHWARD_DIST
GRP_BM.description: Distance N-S from the site reference point. South of the reference point is negative.
GRP_BM.explanation: Measure the north-south distance from the site reference point (see Site Description Instruction). Use magnetic north as a reference. This variable can be reported only (and is mandatory) with BM_TYPE "Installation" and together with BM_NORTHREF, BM_EASTWARD_DIST and BM_HEIGHT

GRP_BM.name: BM_NORTHREF
GRP_BM.explanation: Specify if the North reference used to report the position of the sensors is the Magnetic or the Geographic/True

choices.description: Angles or distances respect to Magnetic North
Angles or distances respect to True North (corrected for the magnetic declination)

GRP_BM.name: BM_SAMPLING_INT
GRP_BM.explanation: Report the time in seconds between two consecutive measurements. This corresponds to the interval between two consecuitve records in the raw data files. This variable can be reported only together with the BM_VARIABLE_H_V_R, BM_LOGGER and BM_FILE (all of them) and with BM_TYPE either "Installation" or "Variable map"

GRP_BM.name: BM_INST_HEAT
GRP_BM.explanation:
Report only in case the sensor is heated. Can be submitted only when BM_TYPE is "Installation" or "Maintenance" in case added in a second stage. Details can be provided in the COMMENT.
If left empty is considered as No. Use "No" in case the Heating is removed (so after the communication of an heating in place)

choices.description: For no just leave empty
Use this if it was Yes before and then changed.

GRP_BM.name: BM_INST_SHIELDING
GRP_BM.explanation:
Report only in case the sensor is shielded reporting the type using the LIST. Can be submitted only when BM_TYPE is "Installation" or "Maintenance" in case added in a second stage. Details can be provided in the COMMENT.
If left empty is considered as No. Use "None" in case the shielding is removed (so after the communication of a Shielding in place)

choices.description: Sensor protected from air temperature changes (heated and not heated)
Sensor protected from direct radiation
Sensor protected from rain and precipitation in general
Sensor protected from direct wind exposure
Use this if there was and Shielding before and then removed.

GRP_BM.name: BM_INST_ASPIRATION
GRP_BM.explanation:
Report only in case the sensor is aspirated reporting the type using the LIST. Can be submitted only when BM_TYPE is "Installation" or "Maintenance" in case added in a second stage. Details can be provided in the COMMENT.
If left empty is considered as No. Use "None" in case the Aspiration is removed (so after the communication of an Aspiration in place).

choices.description: Ventilation based on natural flow of air, without any pump or fan
Ventilation based on a  fan or a pump or any other powered system
Use this if there was and Aspiration before and then removed.

GRP_BM.name: BM_LOGGER
GRP_BM.description: ID of the Logger where variable is registered (the LN value used in the file name)
GRP_BM.explanation: Report here the ID number logger (specified in the LOGGER group) where the measurements made by the instrument are registered. The file name requires two digits but in this variable report only the integer value (e.g. for "L03" in filename report 3). This variable can be reported only together with the BM_VARIABLE_H_V_R, BM_SAMPLING_INT and BM_FILE (all of them) and with BM_TYPE either "Installation" or "Variable map"

GRP_BM.name: BM_FILE
GRP_BM.description: ID of the File where variable is registered (the FN value used in the file name)
GRP_BM.explanation: Report here the ID number of the file (specified in the FILE group) where the measurements made by the instrument are registered. The file name requires two digits but in this variable report only the integer value (e.g. for "F03" in filename report 3). This variable can be reported only together with the BM_VARIABLE_H_V_R, BM_SAMPLING_INT and BM_LOGGER (all of them) and with BM_TYPE either "Installation" or "Variable map"

GRP_BM.name: BM_DATE
GRP_BM.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event date
GRP_BM.explanation: Date of validity of the GRP_BM information provided. This is one of the alternatives, the other is DATE_START and DATE_END. It is the only possibility when BM_TYPE is "Installation" or "Removal" or "Variable Map".

GRP_BM.name: BM_DATE_START
GRP_BM.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event start date
GRP_BM.explanation: In case the BM_TYPE event reported covers a period that is relevant to report, use this variable to indicate the start of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_END and is alternative to DATE. It can not be used when BM_TYPE is "Installation" or "Removal" or "Variable Map"

GRP_BM.name: BM_DATE_END
GRP_BM.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event end date
GRP_BM.explanation: In case the BM_TYPE event reported covers a period that is relevant to report, use this variable to indicate the end of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_START and is alternative to DATE. It can not be used when BM_TYPE is "Installation" or "Removal" or "Variable Map"

GRP_BM.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event comments

GRP_IGBP.name: IGBP
GRP_IGBP.description: Vegetation type based on the IGBP definition
GRP_IGBP.explanation: Please read the class description carefully before selecting the most appropriate IGBP (International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme) category in the predefined list. If the IGBP category that you selected does not adequately represent your site, explain in the IGBP_COMMENT, which is free text.

choices.description: Barren Sparse Vegetation: Lands exposed soil, sand, or rocks and has less than 10% vegetative cover during any time of the year.

Croplands: Lands covered with temporary crops followed by harvest and a bare soil period (e.g., single and multiple cropping systems). Note that perennial woody crops will be classified as the appropriate forest or shrub land cover type.
Closed Shrublands: Lands with woody vegetation less than 2 meters tall and with shrub canopy cover >60%. The shrub foliage can be either evergreen or deciduous.
Cropland/Natural Vegetation Mosaics: Lands with a mosaic of croplands, forest, shrublands, and grasslands in which no one component comprises more than 60% of the landscape

Deciduous Broadleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters.  Consists of broadleaf tree communities with an annual cycle of leaf-on and leaf-off periods.

Deciduous Needleleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters.  Consists of seasonal needleleaf tree communities with an annual cycle of leaf-on and leaf-off periods.

Evergreen Broadleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters. Almost all trees and shrubs remain green year round. Canopy is never without green foliage.

Evergreen Needleleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters. Almost all trees remain green all year. Canopy is never without green foliage.

Grasslands: Lands with herbaceous types of cover. Tree and shrub cover is less than 10%. Permanent wetlands lands with a permanent mixture of water and herbaceous or woody vegetation. The vegetation can be present in either salt, brackish, or fresh water.

Mixed Forests: Lands dominated by trees with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters.  Consists of tree communities with interspersed mixtures or mosaics of the other four forest types.  None of the forest types exceeds 60% of landscape.
Open Shrublands: Lands with woody vegetation less than 2 meters tall and with shrub canopy cover between 10-60%. The shrub foliage can be either evergreen or deciduous.
Savannas: Lands with herbaceous and other understory systems, and with forest canopy cover between 10-30%. The forest cover height exceeds 2 meters.
Snow and Ice: Lands under snow/ice cover most of the year.
Urban and Built-Up Lands: Land covered by buildings and other man-made structures.
Water Bodies : Oceans, seas, lakes, reservoirs, and rivers. Can be either fresh or salt- water bodies.
Permanent Wetlands: Lands with a permanent mixture of water and herbaceous or woody vegetation that cover extensive areas. The vegetation can be present in either salt, brackish, or fresh water
Woody Savannas: Lands with herbaceous and other understory systems, and with forest canopy cover between 30-60%. The forest cover height exceeds 2 meters.

GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.name: FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_METHOD
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.description: Method used to measure the flux variables
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.explanation: Method used to measure the flux of the variable reported in FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_VARIABLE. Use the predefined list. Report different variable-method combinations in different columns (e.g., one column for CO2 flux using eddy covariance, one for CO2 flux using chambers, one for H2O with eddy covariance, etc.).

GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.name: FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_VARIABLE
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.explanation: Use the predefined list of flux variables to report the flux variable that is measured.

GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.name: FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_DATE_START
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.description: Date when data collection for the reported flux variable/method started
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.explanation: The first date of any measurements of the flux variable with the indicated method. Please report the start date at the precision known. Allowed reporting precision are YYYY, YYYYMMDD, and YYYYMMDDHHMM.

GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.name: FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_DATE_END
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.description: Date when data collection for the reported flux variable/method ended
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.explanation: The end date should only be specified when no current or future measurements of the flux variable with the indicated method are planned. Please report the end date at the precision known. Allowed reporting precision are YYYY, YYYYMMDD, and YYYYMMDDHHMM.

GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.name: FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_OPERATIONS
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.explanation: Use the predefined list of status options to report the way this variable-method combination is collected (e.g. continuously).

choices.description: Variable collected continuously with the reported method.
Variable collected only during the growing season with the reported method
Variable collected intermittently with the reported method
Variable collected part of the year with the reported method
The site or equipment to collect the specific variable is not yet operational

GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.name: FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_COMMENT
GRP_FLUX_MEASUREMENTS.explanation: Provide explanatory comments, particularly if "Other" has been selected in the FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_VARIABLE or FLUX_MEASUREMENTS_METHOD variables.

GRP_DM.name: DM_DATE
GRP_DM.description: Date of site disturbance
GRP_DM.explanation: Date of the DM event. This is one of the alternatives that can be also associated with an uncertainty using DATE_UNC. The other possibility is the use of DATE_START and DATE_END

GRP_DM.name: DM_DATE_START
GRP_DM.description: Start date of site disturbance
GRP_DM.explanation: In case DM event reported covers a period, use this variable to indicate the start of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_END and is alternative to DATE.

GRP_DM.name: DM_DATE_END
GRP_DM.description: End date of site disturbance
GRP_DM.explanation: In case DM event reported covers a period, use this variable to indicate the end of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_START and is alternative to DATE.

GRP_DM.name: DM_DATE_UNC
GRP_DM.description: Uncertainty in the End date of site disturbance

GRP_DM.name: DM_COMMENT
GRP_DM.description: Site disturbance comments

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_SN
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Serial number or other unique text string used to identify this instrument
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the serial number of the instrument (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station)

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_TYPE
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument operations and maintenance type
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation:
Report the type of operation, maintenance or event performed/happened to the instrument using the LIST options. This variable is linked to the others in the group. The aim of the variable when reporting a maintenance, a calibration or a disturbance is only to identify the period where measurements can be affected.
In case of Firmware update the new firmware code should be submitted using the INST_FIRMWARE variable.
The first operation must be always the Installation, see the BADM FAQ for more info.

choices.description: Disturbance to the instrument
Calibration of an instrument in the field that changed the instrument calibration
Calibration of an instrument in the field that did not change the instrument calibration
Cleaning an instrument or its parts
Change filter of gas analyser
Firmware update
Use this to report a general comment not fitting with the other options
Installation of an instrument in the field
General maintenance of instrument
Replacement of parts of instruments
Removal of an instrument from the station
Change tube of gas analyser
Mapping of the instrument to one variable

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_DATE
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument operations and maintenance event date

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_DATE_UNC
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Uncertainty in the Instrument operations and maintenance event date

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_DATE_START
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event start date
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: In case the INSTMAN_TYPE event reported covers a period that is relevant to report, use this variable to indicate the start of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_END and is alternative to DATE. It can not be used when INSTMAN_TYPE is Installation or Removal

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_DATE_END
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event end date
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: In case the INSTMAN_TYPE event reported covers a period that is relevant to report, use this variable to indicate the start of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_START and is alternative to DATE. It can not be used when INSTMAN_TYPE is Installation or Removal

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_COMMENT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument operations and maintenance event comments
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report any information relevant to the event that was not reported in other variables.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_VARIABLE_H_V_R
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Variable code suffixed by positional indices (required for map events)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report here the measured variable that is linked to this instrument model and serial number reported in the INSTMAN_MODEL and INSTMAN_SN. The variable name must be identical to the one used in the data submission and composed by the variable code and suffixes indicating the position e.g. TS_1_1_1 (see data submission instructions). For the fluxes it is not mandatory to report if there is only one EC system.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_HEIGHT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Meters above/below ground level (negative values: below ground)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Select the ground reference level as the soil-litter interface at the location the instrument is deployed.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_EASTWARD_DIST
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Distance E-W from the site reference point. West of the reference point is negative
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Measure the east-west distance from the site reference point (the latitude and longitude reported in the Site General Info template) to the instrument with GPS, tape and compass, or other method. Use magnetic north as a reference.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_NORTHWARD_DIST
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Distance N-S from the site reference point. South of the reference point is negative
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Measure the north-south distance from the site reference point (the latitude and longitude reported in the Site General Info template) to the instrument with GPS, tape and compass, or other method. Use magnetic north as a reference.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_NORTHREF
GRP_INSTMAN.description: North reference used (magnetic or geographic)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Specify if the North reference used to report the position of the sensors is the Magnetic or the Geographic/True

choices.description: Angles or distances respect to Magnetic North
Angles or distances respect to True North (corrected for the magnetic declination)

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_SAMPLING_INT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Measurement sampling interval
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the average time in seconds between two measurements. This can be different from the resolution of the output data if averaging is performed in the data logger; if they are different, INSTMAN_AVERAGING_INT should also be reported.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_AVERAGING_INT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Averaging interval for data from data logger
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the averaging interval of the data logger in case measurements are made at higher frequency and then averaged in the logger. Leave blank if no averaging at the logger.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_HEAT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument heating
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation:
Report if the instrument is heated (also if only one part of the sensor if heated). In case of heating of the intake tube of a closed path gas analyzer, use the INSTMAN_GA_CP_TUBE_THERM variable. Use INSTMAN_COMMENT to give more details if needed.
If left empty is considered as No. Use "No" in case the Heating is removed (so after the communication of an heating in place)

choices.description: Use this if it was Yes before and then changed.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_SHIELDING
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument shielding such as radiation, rain, or none
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation:
Use this variable to report if the instrument or part of the instrument is shielded or insulated. Additional details can be provided using the INSTMAN_COMMENT variable. Use INSTMAN_COMMENT to give more details if needed.
If left empty is considered as No. Use "None" in case the shielding is removed (so after the communication of a Shielding in place)

choices.description: Use this if there was and Shielding before and then removed.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_ASPIRATION
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Instrument aspiration such as natural, mechanical, or none
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation:
Report if a flow of air is present in the instrument and if this is natural (ventilation) (e.g. thanks to temperature gradients or wind), or if it is mechanical (e.g. with a pump). Use INSTMAN_COMMENT to give more details if needed.
If left empty is considered as No. Use "None" in case the Aspiration is removed (so after the communication of an Aspiration in place)

choices.description: Use this if there was and Aspiration before and then removed.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_SA_OFFSET_NORTH
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Orientation of the instrument from magnetic north (0-359 degrees)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Azimuth angle of the orientation of the sonic anemometer from magnetic north.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_SA_WIND_FORMAT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Format used in reporting wind components
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the format of the wind measurements performed by the sonic anemometer.

choices.description: Axis velocities
Horizontal angle and vertical
2D horizontal, 1D vertical

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_SA_GILL_ALIGN
GRP_INSTMAN.description: North alignment format for Gill brand anemometers
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: When a Gill anemometer is used, specify the north alignment format. Leave blank for other anemometers.

choices.description: Axis is oriented North
Spar is oriented North

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_FILTERS
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Describe the number and sizes of the closed path filters (closed path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the number, type, size and position of the filters used along the tube for closed path analyzers used in the calculation of fluxes via eddy covariance.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_TUBE_LENGTH
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Tube length (closed path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Length of the tube from the intake to the gas analyzer for closed path analyzers used in the calculation of fluxes via eddy covariance.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_TUBE_IN_DIAM
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Tube inner diameter (closed path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Internal diameter of the intake tube for closed path gas analyzers used in the calculation of fluxes via eddy covariance.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_TUBE_MAT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Tube material (closed path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the material of the gas analyzer intake tube for closed path gas analyzers used in the calculation of fluxes via eddy covariance.

choices.description: Glass tube
Metal, for example Stainless Steel
Other tubing material (that is in contact with the gas). Report additional details in INST_COMMENT
Minimally absorptive synthetic or polymer material, for example Teflon, Silicon-based composite materials, and Synflex

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_TUBE_THERM
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Tube thermal treatment (closed path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report if the intake tube is insulated or insulated+heated for closed path gas analyzers used in the calculation of fluxes via eddy covariance.

choices.description: Heating installed
Insulation only
No thermal treatment

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_FLOW_RATE
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Nominal tube flow rate in the GA tube (closed path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the nominal flow rate of the gas analyzer intake for closed path gas analyzers used in the calculation of fluxes via eddy covariance.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CP_MFC
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Yes if the mass flow controller (MFC) is present (closed path only)

choices.description: Use this if it was Yes before and then changed.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_OP_AZIM_MOUNT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Azimuth angle from north of the gas analyzer as installed (open path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: Report the azimuth of the open path gas analyzer (not the arm). Not needed when INSTMAN_GA_OP_VERT_MOUNT is zero.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_OP_VERT_MOUNT
GRP_INSTMAN.description: Angle with respect to vertical (zenith angle) of gas analyzer as installed (open path only)
GRP_INSTMAN.explanation: For open path gas analyzers only. Equal to zero for vertical installation of open path gas analyzer.

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CO2_ZERO
GRP_INSTMAN.description: The zero CO2 reading for the CO2 free cylinder in a calibration operation

GRP_INSTMAN.name: INSTMAN_GA_CO2_OFFSET

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_SN_1
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: Serial number or other unique text string used to identify this instrument
GRP_INSTPAIR.explanation: Report the serial number of the sensor in order to identify it in the future and relate it to the measured and submitted variable. If the sensor doesn't have a serial number, a number can be assigned by the PI and kept linked univocally to the sensor. A PI assigned S/N should start with either the site code or an acronym related to the institution (e.g. LBNL12345). It must be unique across the entire network.

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_MODEL_2
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: Manufacturer and/or model, or type of instrument
GRP_INSTPAIR.explanation: Select from the LIST INST_MODEL the most precise definition of the sensor used. If it is not available in the list, please contact the regional network for support and evaluate the addition of a new code.

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_SN_2
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: Serial number or other unique text string used to identify this instrument
GRP_INSTPAIR.explanation: Report the serial number of the sensor in order to identify it in the future and relate it to the measured and submitted variable. If the sensor doesn't have a serial number, a number can be assigned by the PI and kept linked univocally to the sensor. A PI assigned S/N should start with either the site code or an acronym related to the institution (e.g. LBNL12345). It must be unique across the entire network.

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_DATE_UNC
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: Uncertainty in the Instrument pair date

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_HEIGHT_SEP
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: The vertical separation between the instrument pair (negative values: instrument 2 is above instrument 1)
GRP_INSTPAIR.explanation: Report the vertical separation between a pair of instruments used together to produce a variable. For example, report vertical separation between a sonic anemometer and gas analyzer used to produce the variable FC (CO2 flux).

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_EASTWARD_SEP
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: The E-W separation between the instrument pair (negative values: instrument 2 is west of instrument 1)
GRP_INSTPAIR.explanation: Report the east-west distance between a pair of instruments used together to produce a variable as measured via GPS, tape and compass, or other method. Use magnetic north as a reference. For example, report E-W separation between a sonic anemometer and gas analyzer used to produce the variable FC (CO2 flux).

GRP_INSTPAIR.name: INSTPAIR_NORTHWARD_SEP
GRP_INSTPAIR.description: The N-S separation between the instrument pair (negative values: instrument 2 is south of instrument 1)
GRP_INSTPAIR.explanation: Report the north-south distance between a pair of instruments used together to produce a variable as measured via GPS, tape and compass, or other method. Use magnetic north as a reference. For example, report N-S separation between a sonic anemometer and gas analyzer used to produce the variable FC (CO2 flux).

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_PLOT
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Unique code of the CP or SP where the litter is measured
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: It is not possible to submit this group for Mires. LITTERPNT_PLOT is linked to the PLOT_ID defined in the Sampling Scheme where the litter is measured. It is a string followed by "_##"  where ## is the numeric ID (e.g. CP_01, or SP-I_01, always two digits). In case of SP-II-order points the numeric ID is composed by two numbers (##-$$) of two digits each where the first identifies the SP-I reference point (e.g. SP-II_01-02)

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_ID
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest: ID of the location inside the CP where litter is measured. See explanation.
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation:
Only Forest. For litter trap report here the ID of the location inside the CP as defined in the Instruction on Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest. For coarse litter, report the ID of the transect (value 1, 2, 3 for transect angle of 0°, 120° or 240° respectively)
In case the location and the trap area remain stable in time, report the LITTERPNT_ID together with the position (using either LITTERPNT_EASTWARD_DIST and LITTERPNT_NORTHWARD_DIST or LITTERPNT_DISTANCE_POLAR and LITTERPNT_ANGLE_POLAR) and the LITTERPNT_AREA once. After that, for the different measurements, report only LITTERPNT_PLOT and LITTERPNT_ID.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_AREA
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Area sampled for litter measurement (frame or trap)
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Report the area of the litter trap or the frame used to collect the litter or residual material. For forest: if stable in time report only in the first submission (see LITTERPNT_ID explanation). Don't report for coarse wood in Forest.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_EASTWARD_DIST
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest: distance E-W between the litter measurement location and the centre of the CP
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest. Only for litter traps. Distance E-W between the litter trap position and the centre of the CP. WEST of the reference point is negative. This variable must be submitted together with LITTERPNT_NORTHWARD_DIST and as alterative to LITTERPNT_DISTANCE_POLAR and LITTERPNT_ANGLE_POLAR. If stable in time report only in the first submission (see LITTERPNT_ID explanation).

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_NORTHWARD_DIST
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest: distance N-S between the litter measurement location and the centre of the CP
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest. Only for litter traps. Distance N-S between the litter trap position and the centre of the CP. SOUTH of the reference point is negative. This variable must be submitted together with LITTERPNT_EASTWARD_DIST and as alterative to LITTERPNT_DISTANCE_POLAR and LITTERPNT_ANGLE_POLAR. If stable in time report only in the first submission (see LITTERPNT_ID explanation).

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_DISTANCE_POLAR
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest: distance between the litter measurement location and the centre of the CP
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest. Only for litter traps. Distance, always positive, between the litter trap position and the centre of the CP. This variable must be submitted together with LITTERPNT_ANGLE_POLAR and as alterative to LITTERPNT_NORTHWARD_DIST and LITTERPNT_EASTWARD_DIST. If stable in time report only in the first submission (see LITTERPNT_ID explanation).

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_ANGLE_POLAR
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest: angle respect to N of the line centre CP – litter measurement location
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest. Only for litter traps. Angle respect to true North (0-360) of the litter trap position respect to the centre of the CP. This variable must be submitted together with LITTERPNT_DISTANCE_POLAR and as alterative to LITTERPNT_NORTHWARD_DIST and LITTERPNT_EASTWARD_DIST. If stable in time report only in the first submission (see LITTERPNT_ID explanation).

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_TYPE
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Type or component of the litter that is reported
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Report the type of litter reported selecting one of the options available in the LIST(LITTYPE)

choices.description: Only Cropland and Grassland. Natural litter during the growing season.
Only Cropland and Grassland. Residuals after harvesting.
Only Forest. Material collected from litter trap (specify the components using LITTER_FRACTION)
Only Forest. Material with diameter between 2 and 10 cm collected with the frame
Only Forest. Coarse litter monitored using the rope (see Instructions)

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_FRACTION
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Fraction or functional group of the measured litter
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest when LITTERPNT_TYPE = non-woody, and for Crop. Fraction or functional group for which litter is measured and reported. If the measurement is done without distinction among fractions or functional groups leave empty. Refer to the Instructions for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements related to the ecosystem monitored to check the options requested. Select one of the options available in the LIST(LITFRAC)

choices.description: Crop species (only Cropland. The species is reported using the SPP group)

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_SPP
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Species for which the litter is measured and reported. For Forest only when LITTERPNT_FRACTION=leaves.
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Mandatory in Forest and LITTERPNT_FRACTION=leaves. When the litter is measured per species (please refer to the Instruction documents on Ancillary Vegetation), report the species following the format explained in the Instructions for Plant Species Reporting. If impossible to identify even the genus report -9999

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Litter value corrected for area (litter mass per square metre)
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation:
Litter measured and calculated following the method described in the Instruction for Ancillary Vegetation Measurement related to the ecosystem monitored. Litter values measured per plot or trap should be scaled to area to report litter mass per square metre (units gDM m-2). Reported for different combinations of LITTERPNT_FRACTION, LITTERPNT_PTYPE and LITTERPNT_SPP (see the Instructions). In case the litter trap didn't collect material due to an evident disturbance report -9999. Add comment with reason of disturbance. In case no litter is found without disturbance, report as zero.
Mandatory variable, alternative to the LITTERPNT_COARSE group.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_LEAVESAREA
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest and LITTERPNT_FRACTION=leaves. Area of the leaves weighted (for LMA calculation)
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest and LITTERPNT_FRACTION=leaves. Total area of the leaves collected in the litter trap with ID = 2 and used to calculate the LMA ratio (see Instructions). Note: this value is not rescaled per square meter.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_COARSE_DIAM
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest and LITTERPNT_TYPE=Coarse. Diameter of the coarse woody material crossing the rope
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest and when LITTERPNT_CLASS = Coarse. It is defined Coarse if the diameter is > 10cm. See Instruction for more information. When submitted must be together with the other three LITTERPNT_COARSE variables.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_COARSE_LENGTH
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest and LITTERPNT_TYPE=Coarse. Length of the coarse woody material crossing the rope
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest and when LITTERPNT_CLASS = Coarse. It is defined Coarse if the diameter is > 10cm. See Instruction for more information. When submitted must be together with the other three LITTERPNT_COARSE variables.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_COARSE_ANGLE
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest and LITTERPNT_TYPE=Coarse. Angle between coarse woody material and the rope (crossed)
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest and when LITTERPNT_CLASS = Coarse. It is defined Coarse if the diameter is > 10cm. See Instruction for more information. When submitted must be together with the other three LITTERPNT_COARSE variables.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_COARSE_DECAY
GRP_LITTERPNT.description: Only Forest and LITTERPNT_TYPE=Coarse. Decay class the coarse woody material crossing the rope
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Only Forest and when LITTERPNT_CLASS = Coarse. It is defined Coarse if the diameter is > 10cm. Values between 1 and 5 accepted as defined in Table 1 of the Instruction on Ancillary Measurements in Forest. When submitted must be together with the other three LITTERPNT_COARSE variables.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_COMMENT
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Use this variable also to give additional information and details about the litter measurement.

GRP_LITTERPNT.name: LITTERPNT_DATE
GRP_LITTERPNT.explanation: Date of  the litter measurement (collection in the field).

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_PLOT
GRP_TREE.description: Unique code of the CP or SP-I where the tree is located
GRP_TREE.explanation: TREE_PLOT is linked to the PLOT_ID defined in the Sampling Scheme where the TREE characteristics are measured. It is a string followed by "_##"  where ## is the numeric ID (e.g. CP_01, or SP-I_01, always two digits). In case of trees outside the CP that are selected for foliar sampling report Outside_CP

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_ID
GRP_TREE.description: Unique ID assigned to the Tree
GRP_TREE.explanation: Mandatory for trees in the CP or for trees selected for foliar sampling that are outside the CP. Possible also for the trees in the SP if needed. Unique ID that is assigned to each tree present in the CP/SP. The ID must be unique inside the same CP/SP (i.e. the same ID can be used in different CPs). For trees outside the CPs (when TREE_PLOT = Outside_CP) the ID must be also unique.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_EASTWARD_DIST
GRP_TREE.description: Distance E-W between the tree and the centre of the CP
GRP_TREE.explanation: Mandatory for trees in the CP or for trees selected for foliar sampling that are outside the CP. Distance E-W between the tree and the centre of the CP (between tree and tower coordinates in case TREE_PLOT = Outside_CP). WEST of the reference point is negative. This variable must be submitted together with TREE_NORTHWARD_DIST and as alterative to TREE_DISTANCE_POLAR and TREE_ANGLE_POLAR.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_NORTHWARD_DIST
GRP_TREE.description: Distance N-S between the tree and the centre of the CP
GRP_TREE.explanation: Mandatory  for trees in the CP or for trees selected for foliar sampling that are outside the CP. Distance N-S between the tree and the centre of the CP (between tree and tower coordinates in case TREE_PLOT = Outside_CP). SOUTH of the reference point is negative. This variable must be submitted together with TREE_EASTWARD_DIST and as alterative to TREE_DISTANCE_POLAR and TREE_ANGLE_POLAR.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_DISTANCE_POLAR
GRP_TREE.description: Distance between the tree and the centre of the CP
GRP_TREE.explanation: Mandatory for trees in the CP or for trees selected for foliar sampling that are outside the CP. Distance, always positive, between the tree and the centre of the CP (between tree and tower coordinates in case TREE_PLOT = Outside_CP). This variable must be submitted together with TREE_ANGLE_POLAR and as alterative to TREE_NORTHWARD_DIST and TREE_EASTWARD_DIST.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_ANGLE_POLAR
GRP_TREE.description: Angle respect to N of the line centre CP – tree
GRP_TREE.explanation: Mandatory for trees in the CP or for trees selected for foliar sampling that are outside the CP. Angle respect to true North (0-360) of the tree position respect to the centre of the CP (of the tree respect to the tower in case TREE_PLOT = Outside_CP). This variable must be submitted together with TREE_DISTANCE_POLAR and as alterative to TREE_NORTHWARD_DIST and TREE_EASTWARD_DIST.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_VARMAP
GRP_TREE.explanation: Report the continuous variable associated to the automatic dendrometer if it is installed on the tree reported. The variable mapped must be associated to a data file of continuous data and identified by the correct variable code (see Instruction on Meteo Data Format). If there is no automatic dendrometer, leave empty.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_DBH
GRP_TREE.explanation: Tree diameter at breast height (DBH) measured following the Instructions for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_STUMP
GRP_TREE.description: ID associated to trees sharing the same stump or root system
GRP_TREE.explanation: Numeric ID that links trees sharing the same root system or stump (e.g. in case of coppice or bifurcated trees). Report the same ID, starting from 1, to all the trees sharing the roots. The ID can be repeated in different CP or SP to report different trees (i.e. ID =1 can be used in both CP_01 and CP_02). In case of single tree leave it empty.

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_HEIGHT
GRP_TREE.explanation: Tree height measured following the Instructions for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_SPP
GRP_TREE.explanation: Species of the tree reported. Follow the format explained in the Instructions for Plant Species Reporting

GRP_TREE.name: TREE_STATUS
GRP_TREE.description: Health status of the tree or tree removal
GRP_TREE.explanation: Report the health status of the tree selecting one of the options available in the LIST. Use this variable also to report if a tree in the CP that was previously reported fallen or is removed, using TREE_ID to identify which tree specifically.

choices.description: see Instruction for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest for definition
see Instruction for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest for definition
see Instruction for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest for definition
see Instruction for Ancillary Vegetation Measurements in Forest for definition
Use this when the tree that was listed fallen on ground and is left there
Use this when the tree that was listed has been removed (harvested)

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O
GRP_SPP.description: Overstory species (taxa)
GRP_SPP.explanation: Overstory vegetation species occurring at the tower site. To enter a plant species, use the scientific name (Genus species Author or Genus Author). Please refer to www.theplantlist.org for current scientific names and authors. For ecosystems without clear over and understory distinctions, use the overstory (O) variables. Do not use SPP_O if reporting SPP_O_VEGTYPE.

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O_VEGTYPE
GRP_SPP.description: Overstory vegetation type
GRP_SPP.explanation: Overstory vegetation type occurring at the tower site. Use predefined list. If vegetation type is not in predefined list, enter "Other/Not in list" and describe briefly in Approach. For ecosystems without clear over and understory distinctions, use the overstory (O) variables. Do not use SPP_O_VEGTYPE if reporting SPP_O.

choices.description: Grasses, Sedges, Rushes, and other grass-like monocots (member of order Poales)
Trees that shed their entire canopy seasonally. Drought or cold avoidance are common reasons for deciduousness.
Trees that do not seasonally shed their full canopies.
All the plants that leave in the understory
Cactus, Euphorbs, including CAM
Moss, lichen

Only use this option if a major vegetation group is not included already included in the predefined list. If an existing vegetation group is not specific enough, use the existing vegetation option and add details in Approach (rather than using the "Other/Not in list" option).
Bare ground, water, or rock. Use only with SPP_PERC_O and SPP_PERC_U
Water (perennially submerged ground)

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O_PREVALENCE
GRP_SPP.description: Overstory species or vegetation type prevalence at site
GRP_SPP.explanation: The prevalence or commonness for the reported species or vegtype in the overstory vegetation. Either SPP_O (the taxa) or SPP_O_VEGTYPE must be specified, not both. For ecosystems without clear over and understory distinctions, use the overstory (O) variables. Do not use SPP_O_PREVALENCE if reporting SPP_O_PERC.

choices.description: Species or vegetation type is one of the major vegetation components at the site
Species or vegetation type is present at the site
Species or vegetation type is rare at site

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O_PERC
GRP_SPP.description: Overstory species or vegetation type percent cover (by mass, number, estimated abundance, or area)
GRP_SPP.explanation: The percent cover for the reported species or vegtype in the overstory vegetation. Either SPP_O (the taxa) or SPP_O_VEGTYPE must be specified, not both. For ecosystems without clear over and understory distinctions, use the overstory (O) variables. The percent cover can be reported by mass, number, estimated abundance, or area and must be defined in the SPP_PERC_UNIT variable. Do not use SPP_O_PERC if reporting SPP_O_PREVALENCE.

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O_PERC_STATISTIC
GRP_SPP.description: Overstory species or vegetation type percent cover statistic
GRP_SPP.explanation: The statistic for the measurement reported. Use only if SPP_O_PERC is reported. Use predefined list (e.g., mean, min / max, standard deviation, etc).

choices.description: Minimum value
Quantile at 1% of distribution
Quantile at 5% of distribution
Quantile at 10% of distribution
Quantile at 25% of distribution
Median - Quantile at 50% of distribution
Quantile at 75% of distribution
Quantile at 90% of distribution
Quantile at 95% of distribution
Quantile at 99% of distribution
Maximum value
Average (mean) value of sample population
Standard deviation may be reported from a sample population that consists of individual or aggregated samples (observations). If the distinction is important, specify in Comments.

Report uncertainty as a plus or minus value in the measurement units. For example, enter 1.5 for +/- 1.5 units. Uncertainty may be reported from the instrument's specifications, determined empirically, or estimated by the tower team. Please describe such details in Approach. For uncertainty values that are better described by a range, a percent, or other, please enter information in Comments.
Single observation

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O_PERC_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_SPP.description: Overstory species or vegetation type percent cover statistic method
GRP_SPP.explanation: Method used to generate the reported statistic (e.g., aggregate of individuals, aggregate of sample aggregates) from observations representing the same time period. Use predefined list. The aggregation method is not meant to describe temporal aggregations for example in calculations of higher frequency observations (e.g., sub-minute) to lower frequency observations (e.g., hourly) at a single location.

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).
Estimate made by expert familiar with site

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_O_PERC_STATISTIC_NUMBER
GRP_SPP.description: Number of observations used to determine overstory species or vegetation type percent cover statistic
GRP_SPP.explanation: Number of observations (samples / replicates) used to calculate the STATISTIC for the reported measurement. Use only if SPP_O_PERC is reported.

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_PERC_UNIT
GRP_SPP.description: Unit of the species or vegetation type percent cover measurement
GRP_SPP.explanation: Use predefined list to indicate whether the percentage cover in SPP_O_PERC and SPP_U_PERC are calculated as 1) mass = dry matter mass of the species or vegetation type / total dry mass, 2) number = number of individuals of the species / total number of individuals, 3) estimated abundance technique such as the pindrop method, or 4) area = land surface covered by the species or vegetation type / total land surface area (i.e., from a top down or bird's eye view). Area totalled across species or vegetation types must sum to equal or less than 100%. Unspecified area, or the difference between the total vegetation area and 100%, will be considered no vegetation (bare ground, water, rock). For forest ecosystems, calculate the area of trees with the area of the tree crown.

choices.description: Percent cover reported as number of individuals of the species or vegetation type per total number of individuals

Area totalled across species or vegetation types must sum to less than 100%. Unspecified area, or the difference between the total vegetation area and 100%, will be considered no vegetation (bare ground, water, rock). For forest ecosystems, calculate the area of trees with the area of the tree crown.

GRP_SPP.explanation: Please report the date at the precision known. Allowed reporting precisions are YYYY, YYYYMM, YYYYMMDD, and YYYYMMDDHHMM. For measurements conducted during a campaign or for temporal averages, use DATE_START and DATE_END instead of DATE.

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_DATE_START
GRP_SPP.description: Start date of species or vegetation type percent cover measurement
GRP_SPP.explanation: Start date of a measurement campaign or start date of a temporal average. Please report the date at the precision known. Allowed reporting precisions are YYYY, YYYYMM, YYYYMMDD, and YYYYMMDDHHMM. Do not use DATE_START if DATE is used.

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_DATE_END

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_DATE_UNC
GRP_SPP.description: Uncertainty in the species or vegetation type percent cover measurement date, start date, and/or end date
GRP_SPP.explanation: If uncertainty in the start date differs than end date, report the uncertainty for start date here in DATE_UNC and the uncertainty for end date in Comments.

GRP_SPP.name: SPP_COMMENT

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Biomass values reported in the units sepecified by BIOMASS_UNIT. Total system biomass (i.e., combined standing, fallen, and detached) should be reported here selecting BIOMASS_STATUS = All. Biomass measures of only material that has fallen or is detached from the organism should be reported in the LITTER_DEBRIS group. Biomass that has been removed by humans (disturbance or management) should be reported in a forthcoming group.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_UNIT
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use predefined list to specify the unit of measurement in dry mass or carbon.

choices.description: kilograms Dry Mass per meter squared
grams Carbon per meter squared

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_STATUS
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use the predefined list to indicate the vegetative status of biomass measured (e.g., all, alive, dead standing, mixed standing). Use the LITTER_DEBRIS group to report biomass measures of only material that has fallen or is no longer attached to the plant.

choices.description: All vegetation: alive or dead; standing or litter / debris (fallen or detached from the plant)

Living plants or components of a plant organism. Includes green plant material, woody or structural components from organisms that are alive, and dormant components like storage bodies and reproductive fruits and seeds.
Standing wood or structural components of a plant organism that are dead, or non-woody components that are dead but still attached to a plant organism.
Living and/or dead components of a standing organism(s). Includes green and dead/dormant foliage and all woody material that are attached to the organism.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_SPP
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Vegetation species being described by the measurement. To enter a plant species, use the scientific name (Genus species Author or Genus Author). Please refer to www.theplantlist.org for current scientific names and authors. If the measurement includes all vegetation present, do not enter a value. Do not use SPP if reporting VEGTYPE.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_VEGTYPE
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use the predefined list to indicate the type of vegetation being described by the measurement (e.g., Grass, Evergreen Tree, Deciduous Tree, etc). If the measurement includes all vegetation present, do not enter a value. If vegetation type is not in predefined list, enter "Other/Not in list" and describe briefly in Approach. Do not use VEGTYPE if reporting SPP.

choices.description: Grasses, Sedges, Rushes, and other grass-like monocots (member of order Poales)
Trees that shed their entire canopy seasonally. Drought or cold avoidance are common reasons for deciduousness.
Trees that do not seasonally shed their full canopies.
All the plants that leave in the understory
Cactus, Euphorbs, including CAM
Moss, lichen

Only use this option if a major vegetation group is not included already included in the predefined list. If an existing vegetation group is not specific enough, use the existing vegetation option and add details in Approach (rather than using the "Other/Not in list" option).
Bare ground, water, or rock. Use only with SPP_PERC_O and SPP_PERC_U
Water (perennially submerged ground)

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_STATISTIC
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: The statistic for the measurement reported. Use predefined list (e.g., mean, min / max, standard deviation, etc).

choices.description: Minimum value
Quantile at 1% of distribution
Quantile at 5% of distribution
Quantile at 10% of distribution
Quantile at 25% of distribution
Median - Quantile at 50% of distribution
Quantile at 75% of distribution
Quantile at 90% of distribution
Quantile at 95% of distribution
Quantile at 99% of distribution
Maximum value
Average (mean) value of sample population
Standard deviation may be reported from a sample population that consists of individual or aggregated samples (observations). If the distinction is important, specify in Comments.

Report uncertainty as a plus or minus value in the measurement units. For example, enter 1.5 for +/- 1.5 units. Uncertainty may be reported from the instrument's specifications, determined empirically, or estimated by the tower team. Please describe such details in Approach. For uncertainty values that are better described by a range, a percent, or other, please enter information in Comments.
Single observation

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Method used to generate the reported statistic (e.g., aggregate of individuals, aggregate of sample aggregates) from observations representing the same time period. Use predefined list. The aggregation method is not meant to describe temporal aggregations for example in calculations of higher frequency observations (e.g., sub-minute) to lower frequency observations (e.g., hourly) at a single location.

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).
Estimate made by expert familiar with site

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_STATISTIC_NUMBER
GRP_BIOMASS.description: Number of observations used to determine Biomass statistics
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Number of observations (samples / replicates) used to calculate the STATISTIC for the reported measurement.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_ORGAN
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Organ or plant component of the biomass measurement if applicable. Use predefined list.

choices.description: Total including above- and belowground (all components)
Total aboveground (all components)
Total belowground (all components)
All woody components including above- and belowground
All aboveground woody components (includes fine and coarse wood)
For alive or dead standing biomass, or debris: Woody material diameter > 10cm. For example, trunks of trees. If another size classification is used, explain in the APPROACH variable.

For alive or dead standing biomass, or litter or debris: woody material with diameter between 2cm - 10cm. For example, stems and branches. If another size classification is used, explain in the APPROACH variable.
Total roots (including rhizoids)
Roots > 2mm diameter. If another size classification is used, explain in APPROACH.
Roots > 2mm diameter and rhizoids. If another size classification is used, explain in APPROACH.
Tubers, rhizomes, bulbs, corms
Reproductive organs prior to maturing. Includes flowers and/or inflorescences (groups of flowers, such as in the sunflower family Asteraceae).
Leaves, needles, fronds, cacti spines
Reproductive bodies like fruits and cones that enclose or support seeds, including grains, kernels, legumes, capsules, utricles, achenes, berries, drupes, pomes.
Only for herbaceous plants with non-woody stems
Only use this option if your organ category is not already included in the predefined list. If an existing organ option is not specific enough, use the existing option and add details in COMMENT.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_GREENNESS

choices.description: Plant material is green (e.g., has chlorophyll)
Plant material is no longer green and in a scenesced or dormant state (e.g., has no chlorophyll)
Part of the plant material is green and part senesced / dormant.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_LIFESTAGE
GRP_BIOMASS.description: Tree lifestage of the biomass measured
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use the predefined list to indicate the tree life stage being described by the measurement (e.g., Seedling, Sapling, etc). If the measurement includes all life stages present, do not enter a value. Use only for biomass measurement of trees.

choices.description: Trees less than 1 year old.
Young tree with diameter at breast height (1.375m) less than 1cm or with height less than breast height (1.375m).

Young tree with diameter at breast height (1.375m) between 1cm and 5cm. When used with the TREE_NUM variable, if the minimum DBH is different than 1cm, use TREES_NUM_DBH_MIN to specify the minimum DBH used to determine this lifestage.

Adult individuals. For trees, diameter at breast height (1.375m) greater than 5cm. When used with the TREE_NUM variable, if the minimum DBH is different than 5cm, use TREES_NUM_DBH_MIN to specify the minimum DBH used to determine this lifestage.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_ROOT_PROFILE_ZERO_REF
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use for root or other belowground biomass measurement. Profile Zero Reference is the horizontal plane from which the soil profile minimum and maximum depths are measured. For example, top of mineral soil or top of litter layer. Use predefined list.

choices.description: Top of mineral soil not including organic layers
On top of all organic layers
See additional information in Approach / Comments

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_ROOT_PROFILE_MIN
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use for root or other belowground biomass measurement. Profile minimum depth is the vertical distance from profile zero reference to the top of soil layer being measured.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_ROOT_PROFILE_MAX
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Use for root or other belowground biomass measurement. Profile maximum depth is the vertical distance from profile zero reference to the bottom of soil layer being measured.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_METHOD
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Method used to quantify the Biomass. Use predefined list. If method is not present, select "Other" and give additional details in BIOMASS_APPROACH.

choices.description: Biomass calculated from an allometric method. Use if none of the other allometric options in the predefined list apply. Add more details in BIOMASS_APPROACH.
Biomass calculated using a site-specific allometric relationship. Add equation if possible in BIOMASS_APPROACH.
Biomass calculated using an allometric relationship from the literature. Add reference if possible in BIOMASS_APPROACH.
Biomass derived from point cloud data aquired by laser scanning from the ground.
Biomass derived from point cloud data aquired by drone or aircraft.
Use if method is not in predefined list. Add details in BIOMASS_APPROACH.

GRP_BIOMASS.name: BIOMASS_APPROACH
GRP_BIOMASS.explanation: Report additional details used to quantify the reported Biomass

Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).

Standard deviation may be reported from a sample population that consists of individual or aggregated samples (observations). If the distinction is important, specify in Comments.

Report uncertainty as a plus or minus value in the measurement units. For example, enter 1.5 for +/- 1.5 units. Uncertainty may be reported from the instrument's specifications, determined empirically, or estimated by the tower team. Please describe such details in Approach. For uncertainty values that are better described by a range, a percent, or other, please enter information in Comments.
Single observation

GRP_SNOW_DEPTH.name: SNOW_DEPTH_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_SNOW_DEPTH.explanation: Method used to generate the reported statistic (e.g., aggregate of individuals, aggregate of sample aggregates) from observations representing the same time period. Use predefined list. The aggregation method is not meant to describe temporal aggregations for example in calculations of higher frequency observations (e.g., sub-minute) to lower frequency observations (e.g., hourly) at a single location.

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).
Estimate made by expert familiar with site
