GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_SN
GRP_STO.description: Serial number or other unique text string used to identify this instrument
GRP_STO.explanation: The serial number of the GA (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station). This variable is mandatory when any of the STO_GA variables is reported.

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_VARIABLE
GRP_STO.description: Variable (gas) measured with the GA used for the storage measurement
GRP_STO.explanation: Select (one of) the measured gas from the options in the respective LIST(STO_VAR), mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation". In case additional variables are measured report them using STO_TYPE = "Variable Map". This variable can be reported only together with STO_LOGGER and STO_FILE. In case STO_GA_SAMPLING_INT is different with respect to 1 second, it must be reported too.

choices.description: Methane, CH4 in nmolmol-1 (ppb)
Carbon dioxide, CO2 in umolmol-1 (ppm)
Water, H2O in mmolmol-1
Nitrous oxide, N2O in nmolmol-1 (ppb)

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_PROF_ID
GRP_STO.description: ID of the profile system used with the GA
GRP_STO.explanation: Report the ID (STO_PROF_ID ) of the profile system used with the reported GA. It can be reported only when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_FLOW_RATE
GRP_STO.description: Nominal flow rate in tube from the buffer to the GA (close path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: The nominal flow rate to the GA (report it even though the actual flow rate is measured and recorded in the data file)

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_SAMPLING_INT
GRP_STO.description: Measurement sampling interval of the gas analyser
GRP_STO.explanation: The time in seconds between two consecutive records as reported in the raw data files. This variable can be reported only if different from 1 second and with the agreement of ETC. In this case, it must be submitted together with the STO_GA_VARIABLE, STO_LOGGER and STO_FILE (all of them) and with STO_TYPE either "GA installation" or "Variable map"

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_AZIM_MOUNT
GRP_STO.description: Azimuth angle from north of the gas analyser as installed (open path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: Only in case an open path is used. This variable can be reported only with STO_CONFIG "Separate". It is mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_VERT_MOUNT
GRP_STO.description: Angle with respect to vertical (zenith angle) of gas analyser as installed (open path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: Only in case an open path is used. This variable can be reported only with STO_CONFIG "Separate". It is mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_TUBE_LENGTH
GRP_STO.description: Length of the tube from the lines switch to the GA (closed path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: Length of the tube from the point where the individual lines are switched to the gas analyser. This point could be the valves system (manifold) exit point in case each line has its own buffer. It could be the exit point of buffer volume in case the buffer is common among the sampling points (simultaneous sampling scheme). It is mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_TUBE_DIAM
GRP_STO.description: Inner diameter of the tube from the lines switch to the GA (closed path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: Diameter of the tube from the point where the individual lines are switched to the gas analyser (see STO_GA_TUBE_LENGTH explanation). It is mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_TUBE_MAT
GRP_STO.description: Material of the tube from the lines switch to the GA (closed path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: Select the material of the tube from the point where the individual lines are switched to the gas analyser (see STO_GA_TUBE_LENGTH explanation) from the options in the respective LIST (STO_TUBEMAT). It is mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

choices.description: Glass tube
Iron tube
Other type of tube
Teflon tube

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_TUBE_THERM
GRP_STO.description: Thermal treatment of the tube from the lines switch to the GA (closed path only)
GRP_STO.explanation: Select the possible thermal treatment of the tube from the point where the individual lines are switched to the gas analyser (see STO_GA_TUBE_LENGTH explanation) from the options in the respective LIST (STO_TUBETHERM). It is mandatory when STO_TYPE = "GA installation"

choices.description: Heating installed
Insulation only
No thermal treatment

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_CAL_VARIABLE
GRP_STO.description: The gas species being calibrated/checked
GRP_STO.explanation: This is the gas species being calibrated or field checked. It can be submitted only when STO_TYPE is either "Field calibration" or "Field calibration check". This variable can be submitted only together with STO_GA_CAL_VALUE and STO_GA_CAL_REF.

choices.description: Methane, CH4 in nmolmol-1 (ppb)
Carbon dioxide, CO2 in umolmol-1 (ppm)
Water, H2O in mmolmol-1
Nitrous oxide, N2O in nmolmol-1 (ppb)

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_CAL_VALUE
GRP_STO.description: The measured value of the reference gas during the field calibration/check
GRP_STO.explanation: These are the readings before any change in the settings and can be submitted only when STO_TYPE is either "Field calibration" or "Field calibration check". This variable can be submitted only together with STO_GA_CAL_VARIABLE and STO_GA_CAL_REF.

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_CAL_REF
GRP_STO.description: The reference concentration of the gas used in the field calibration/check. Put 0 in case of zero calibration/check
GRP_STO.explanation: This is the reference value for the STO_GA_CAL_VARIABLE concentration. In case of zero calibration, report 0. It can be submitted only when STO_TYPE is either "Field calibration" or "Field calibration check". This variable can be submitted only together with STO_GA_CAL_VARIABLE and STO_GA_CAL_VALUE.

GRP_STO.name: STO_GA_CAL_TA
GRP_STO.description: Ambient air temperature where and when the gas analyser was calibrated
GRP_STO.explanation: In case the field calibration happens in a hut report the internal temperature of the hut. It can be submitted only when STO_TYPE is either "Field calibration" or "Field calibration check"

GRP_STO.name: STO_LOGGER
GRP_STO.description: ID of the Logger where variable is registered (the LN value used in the file name)
GRP_STO.explanation: The ID number of the logger (specified in the LOGGER group) where the measurements made by the instrument are registered. Although the code in the file name requires two digits, in this variable report only the integer value (e.g. for "L03" in filename report 3).  This variable can be reported only together with STO_GA_VARIABLE and STO_FILE (both) and with STO_TYPE either "GA installation" or "Variable map"

GRP_STO.name: STO_FILE
GRP_STO.description: ID of the File where variable is registered (the FN value used in the file name)
GRP_STO.explanation: The ID number of the file (specified in the FILE group) where the measurements made by the instrument are registered. Although the code in the file name requires two digits, in this variable report only the integer value (e.g. for "F03" in filename report 3). This variable can be reported only together with STO_GA_VARIABLE and STO_FILE (both) and with STO_TYPE either "GA installation" or "Variable map"

GRP_STO.name: STO_DATE
GRP_STO.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event date
GRP_STO.explanation: Date of validity of the GRP_STO information provided. This is one of the alternatives, the other is DATE_START and DATE_END. It is the only possibility when STO_TYPE is "GA installation", "Level installation", "GA removal", "Level removal" or "Variable Map"

GRP_STO.name: STO_DATE_START
GRP_STO.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event start date
GRP_STO.explanation: In case the STO_TYPE event reported covers a period that is relevant to report, use this variable to indicate the start of the event. This variable must be always associated to DATE_END and is alternative to DATE. It can not be used when STO_TYPE is "GA installation", "Level installation", "GA removal", "Level removal" or "Variable Map"

GRP_STO.name: STO_DATE_END
GRP_STO.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event end date
GRP_STO.explanation: In case the STO_TYPE event reported covers a period that is relevant to report, use this variable to indicate the end of the event. In case the event is still ongoing put the expected end date and then replace it later with the actual end date. This variable must be always associated to DATE_START and is alternative to DATE. It can not be used when STO_TYPE is "GA installation", "Level installation", "GA removal", "Level removal" or "Variable Map"

GRP_STO.name: STO_DATE_UNC
GRP_STO.description: Uncertainty in the date

GRP_STO.name: STO_COMMENT
GRP_STO.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event comments

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_PLOT_ID
GRP_SOSM.description: Unique SP location where the sample has been collected
GRP_SOSM.explanation: The SOSM_PLOT_ID is linked to the SP location defined in the Sampling Scheme. It can be either a SP-I or SP-II location, as function of the type of sample (composite or individual). It must report the official code of the location in the format SP-I_## or SP-II_##-$$ (e.g. SP-I_03 for the composite sample at SP-I_03 or SP-II_01-02 for the individual sample collected at the SP-II location). Refer to the Instruction on Soil Sampling for information on which locations should be used.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_SAMPLE_ID
GRP_SOSM.description: Sample ID reported on the bags (see Instructions)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: The label that is reported on the bag used to collect the soil sample and to send it to the ETC laboratories. Follow the Instruction for the code structure.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT
GRP_SOSM.description: Report if the sample is an Organic, Histic  or a Mineral sample
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Use the LIST options to report if it is an organic soil sample and which layer, a histic soil sample,  or a mineral soil sample. Refer to the Instructions for details.

choices.description: Organic
Organic Oi layer
Organic Oa layer
Organic Oe layer
Mineral soil
Histic soil  (peatland)

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_AREA
GRP_SOSM.description: Area sampled
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Area of the frame in case of Organic sample or first layer of mineral soil, area of the core section for mineral sample.  Only when Individual samples are reported (required).

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_VOLUME
GRP_SOSM.description: Volume of the sample
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only when Individual samples are reported (required).

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_UD
GRP_SOSM.description: Upper sampling depth when core is extracted
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Upper sampling depth to be reported only for mineral and histic soil samples

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_LD
GRP_SOSM.description: Lower sampling depth when core is extracted
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Lower sampling depth to be reported only for mineral and histic soil samples

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_THICKNESS
GRP_SOSM.description: Thickness of the layer sampled when frame is used
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Thickness of the cavity for the organic layer sampled with the frame method as average of multiple single heights measurements (see Instructions). For mineral layer use SOSM_UD and SOSM_LD also in case the frame method is used.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W0
GRP_SOSM.description: Fresh weight of the sample (for organic or total mineral)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Fresh weight of the sample. Using as reference the Instruction on Soil Sampling, when associated to SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT equal to H, O, Oa, Oi or Oe it is equivalent to W0_O, when associated to SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT equal to M is equivalent to W0_T.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W0_OH
GRP_SOSM.description: Fresh weight after removal of coarse elements, mosses, roots, and other living material (only organic samples)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only for organic samples. Fresh weight of the holorganic material sample. Can be used only when SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT is  H, O, Oa, Oi or Oe.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W0_OS
GRP_SOSM.description: Fresh weight of coarse mineral element in the organic sample (only organic samples)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only for organic samples. Fresh weight of the coarse mineral elements included in the organic material sample. Can be used only when SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT is H, O, Oa, Oi or Oe.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W0_OR
GRP_SOSM.description: Fresh weight of roots and living plant material in the organic sample (only organic samples)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only for organic samples. Fresh weight of roots and living plant material included in the organic material sample. Can be used only when SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT is  H, O, Oa, Oi or Oe.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W30
GRP_SOSM.description: Weight after drying at 30°C (for organic or total mineral)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Weight of the sample dried at 30°C. Using as reference the Instruction on Soil Sampling, when associated to SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT equal to H, O, Oa, Oi or Oe it is equivalent to W30_OH (after removal of coarse material, mosses, roots, and other living material), when associated to SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT equal to M is equivalent to W30.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W30_E
GRP_SOSM.description: Weight of fine earth after drying at 30°C (only mineral samples)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only for mineral samples. Weight of the fine earth mineral soil sample dried at 30°C. Can be used only when SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT = M.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W70_R
GRP_SOSM.description: Weight of roots after drying at 70°C (for organic or mineral)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Weight of the roots and living plant material dried at 70°C. Using as reference the Instruction on Soil Sampling, it is equivalent to W70_R.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_W105_S
GRP_SOSM.description: Weight of coarse mineral element after drying at 105°C (for organic or mineral)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Weight of the coarse material included in the sample, dried at 105°C. Using as reference the Instruction on Soil Sampling, it is equivalent to W105_S.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_WX30_E
GRP_SOSM.description: Weight of composite fine earth sample after drying at 30°C  (only mineral samples)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only for mineral samples. Weight of the combined mineral soil sample after quartering, dried at 30°C. Can be used only when SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT = M and it is reported for SP-I locations.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_WX105_E
GRP_SOSM.description: Weight of composite fine earth sample after drying at 105°C (only mineral samples)
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Only for mineral samples. Weight of the combined mineral soil sample after quartering, dried at 105°C. Can be used only when SOSM_SAMPLE_MAT = M and it is reported for SP-I locations.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_COMMENT
GRP_SOSM.description: Soil sampling comments
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Use this variable also to give additional information and details about the method used.

GRP_SOSM.name: SOSM_DATE
GRP_SOSM.description: Soil sampling date
GRP_SOSM.explanation: Date of sampling

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_MODEL
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Model of the camera used. Use the options provided in the LIST(FIELDCAM)

choices.description: Phenocam, StarDot Technologies, NetCam SC 5MP IR (with Day/Night, also named SD500BN), excluding SC 5MP
Phenocam, StarDot Technologies, NetCamLIVE2, excluding NetCamLIVE

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_SN
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Serial number of the camera used. The value must be unique. In case the original SN is not available, create a new one and keep it unique and linked to the specific camera

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_CATEGORY
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Select from the list the category of camera used. The code is the same that should be used in the file name

choices.description: Use this for phenological cameras (Phenocam)
Use this for thermal cameras

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_FOCAL_LENGTH
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Report the focal length of the lens used with the camera, expressed in mm

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_RESOLUTION
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Report the image resolution in the format HxV where H is the horizontal resolution and V is the vertical. For example 1920x1080

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_ID
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: The value is an ID that identifies the combination Camera + Lens and all the parameters. It is used in the file names to link the picture to the system used. It must be unique for each camera-lens combination (in case multiple combinations are used). Maximum 2 digits.

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_TYPE
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Report the type of operation performed, for example the installation or removal, maintenances, disturbances, selecting one option from the LIST(CAMTYPE)

choices.description: Installation of the camera system in the field
Removal of the camera system
Maintenance operation to the camera system. Use CAMERA_COMMENT to give more details
Disturbance happening to the camera system. Use CAMERA_COMMENT to give more details

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_INST_HEIGHT
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Height above ground where the camera is installed. Can be submitted only when CAMERA_TYPE is Installation and together with all the other CAMERA_INST_* variables.

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_INST_EASTWARD_DIST
GRP_CAMERA.description: Distance E-W from the site reference point. West of the reference point is negative.
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Measure the east-west distance from the site reference point (see Site Description Instruction). Can be submitted only when CAMERA_TYPE is Installation and together with all the other CAMERA_INST_* variables.

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_INST_NORTHWARD_DIST
GRP_CAMERA.description: Distance N-S from the site reference point. South of the reference point is negative.
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Measure the north-south distance from the site reference point (see Site Description Instruction). Can be submitted only when CAMERA_TYPE is Installation and together with all the other CAMERA_INST_* variables.

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_INST_DIRECTION
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Horizontal angle (as degrees from N, clockwise) defining the view direction of the camera. Can be submitted only when CAMERA_TYPE is Installation and together with all the other CAMERA_INST_* variables.

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_INST_NORTHREF
GRP_CAMERA.description: North reference used for camera system orientation (magnetic or geographic)
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Specify if the North reference used to report the direction of the camera system (CAMERA_INST_DIRECTION) is the Magnetic or the Geographic/True. Can be submitted only when CAMERA_TYPE is Installation and together with all the other CAMERA_INST_* variables.

choices.description: Angles or distances respect to Magnetic North
Angles or distances respect to True North (corrected for the magnetic declination)

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_INST_VERT_ANGLE
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Specify the angle of view of the camera respect to the horizontal position. If mounted horizontal report 0, if with an inclination toward the ground report a negative angle in degrees. For example if the camera is inclined 15° toward the ground report -15. Can be submitted only when CAMERA_TYPE is Installation and together with all the other CAMERA_INST_* variables.

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_COMMENT
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Comments on the camera system reported

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_DATE_START
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Starting date of the reported camera system information

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_DATE_END
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Ending date of the reported camera system information

GRP_CAMERA.name: CAMERA_DATE
GRP_CAMERA.explanation: Date of the reported camera system information

GRP_EC.name: EC_MODEL
GRP_EC.description: Manufacturer and/or model, or type of instrument
GRP_EC.explanation:
Report the model of the instrument (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station).
Use GA_PUMP-other only in case a pump different respect to the LI-COR Flow Module LI-7200-101 is used.

choices.description: Gas Analyzer (Closed Path), LI-COR LI-7200
Gas Analyzer (Closed Path), LI-COR LI-7200RS
Sonic Anemometer (3D), Gill, HS-100
Sonic Anemometer (3D), Gill, HS-50
Pump for GA, non-LI-COR pump if LI-7200-101 is not used

GRP_EC.name: EC_SN
GRP_EC.description: Serial number or other unique text string used to identify this instrument
GRP_EC.explanation: Report the serial number of the instrument (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station)

GRP_EC.name: EC_TYPE
GRP_EC.description: Operations, maintenance or event happening at the sensor
GRP_EC.explanation:
Report the type of operation, maintenance or event performed/happened to the instrument using the LIST options. This variable is linked to the others in the group. In case of firmware update the new firmware code should be reported using the INST_FIRMWARE variable.
In case of change in logger, file or sampling interval use EC_TYPE = "Maintenance".

choices.description: Disturbance to the instrument
Calibration of an instrument in the field (adjust parameters)
Check of calibration of an instrument in the field
Cleaning an instrument or its parts
Change of the filter in the tube
Firmware update
Installation of the instrument in the field
General maintenance of instrument
Connection failure that didn't allow data transmission (but data are collected)
Replacement of parts of instruments
Removal of an instrument from the station
Use this to report a general comment not fitting with the other options

GRP_EC.name: EC_HEIGHT
GRP_EC.description: Meters aboveground level
GRP_EC.explanation: Use as reference level the organic-mineral horizons boundary or the surface when not possible to identify (see Instruction on Soil Meteo). This variable can be reported (and is mandatory) only with EC_TYPE "Installation" and together with EC_EASTWARD_DIST and EC_NORTHWARD_DIST. If reporting the GA_PUMP-other insert the same location of the LI-COR 7200 intake.

GRP_EC.name: EC_EASTWARD_DIST
GRP_EC.description: Distance E-W from the site reference point. West of the reference point is negative.
GRP_EC.explanation: Measure the east-west distance from the site reference point (see Site Description Instruction). Use magnetic north as a reference. This variable can be reported (and is mandatory) only with EC_TYPE "Installation" and together with EC_HEIGHT and EC_NORTHWARD_DIST. If reporting the GA_PUMP-other insert the same location of the LI-COR 7200 intake.

GRP_EC.name: EC_NORTHWARD_DIST
GRP_EC.description: Distance N-S from the site reference point. South of the reference point is negative.
GRP_EC.explanation: Measure the north-south distance from the site reference point (see Site Description Instruction). Use magnetic north as a reference. This variable can be reported (and is mandatory) only with EC_TYPE "Installation" and together with EC_HEIGHT and EC_EASTWARD_DIST. If reporting the GA_PUMP-other insert the same location of the LI-COR 7200 intake.

GRP_EC.name: EC_NORTHREF
GRP_EC.description: North reference used for EC system position and SA orientation (magnetic or geographic)
GRP_EC.explanation: Specify if the North reference used to report the position of the EC system and the orientation of the SA (EC_SA_OFFSET_N) is the Magnetic or the Geographic/True

choices.description: Angles or distances respect to Magnetic North
Angles or distances respect to True North (corrected for the magnetic declination)

GRP_EC.name: EC_SAMPLING_INT
GRP_EC.description: Measurement sampling interval
GRP_EC.explanation: Report the average time in seconds between two measurements. This variable can be reported only together with the EC_LOGGER and EC_FILE and with EC_TYPE either "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_SA_HEAT
GRP_EC.description: Report only if the sonic anemometer if heated
GRP_EC.explanation: Report only in case the Sonic anemometer is heated (even is occasionally). Can be submitted only (and is mandatory) with EC_TYPE  "Installation" and EC_MODEL either SA-Gill HS-50 or SA-Gill HS-100. Details can be provided in the COMMENT

GRP_EC.name: EC_SA_OFFSET_N
GRP_EC.description: Orientation of the instrument from true North (0-359 degrees)
GRP_EC.explanation: Azimuth angle of the orientation of the sonic anemometer from true North. Can be submitted only (and is mandatory) with EC_TYPE  "Installation" and EC_MODEL either SA-Gill HS-50 or SA-Gill HS-100.

GRP_EC.name: EC_SA_WIND_FORMAT
GRP_EC.description: Format used in reporting wind components
GRP_EC.explanation: Report the format of the wind measurements performed by the sonic anemometer. Can be submitted only EC_MODEL either SA-Gill HS-50 or SA-Gill HS-100 and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

choices.description: Axis velocities
Horizontal angle and vertical
2D horizontal, 1D vertical

GRP_EC.name: EC_SA_GILL_ALIGN
GRP_EC.description: North alignment format
GRP_EC.explanation: Specify the north alignment format. Can be submitted only with EC_MODEL either SA-Gill HS-50 or SA-Gill HS-100 and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

choices.description: Axis is oriented North
Spar is oriented North

GRP_EC.name: EC_SA_GILL_PCI
GRP_EC.description: Report only if the original Gill PCI is used
GRP_EC.explanation: Report if the original Gill PCI is used. Can be submitted only with EC_MODEL either SA-Gill HS-50 or SA-Gill HS-100 and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_FLOW_RATE
GRP_EC.description: Nominal  flow rate in the GA tube
GRP_EC.explanation: Report the nominal flow rate that is used (even if then the actual flow rate is measured). Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200, GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS or GA_PUMP-other (in case of external pump)  and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_LICOR_FM_SN
GRP_EC.description: If used, serial number of the LI-COR flow module (7200-101)
GRP_EC.explanation: In case the original LI-COR flow module is used report the serial number (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station). Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS  and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_LICOR_TP_SN
GRP_EC.description: Tube package number of the LI-COR GA tube mounted
GRP_EC.explanation: Report the package number of the tube used. Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS  and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_LICOR_AIU_SN
GRP_EC.description: Serial number of the Auxiliary Interface Unit used (LI-COR LI-7550 AIU)
GRP_EC.explanation: In case the original LI-COR Auxiliary Interface Unit is used report the serial number (must be one of the models listed in the INST group, in the availability of the station). Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS and with EC_TYPE "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_CAL_CO2_ZERO
GRP_EC.description: The zero CO2 reading for the CO2 free cylinder in a field calibration operation
GRP_EC.explanation: These are the readings prior to any change in the CO2 zero settings. Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS and with EC_TYPE "Field Calibration" or "Field Calibration Check"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_CAL_CO2_OFFSET
GRP_EC.description: The instrument CO2 reading using the reference cylinder in the field calibration operation
GRP_EC.explanation: These are the readings prior to any change in the CO2 span settings. Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS and with EC_TYPE "Field Calibration" or "Field Calibration Check". This variable can be submitted only together with EC_GA_CAL_REF.

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_CAL_CO2_REF
GRP_EC.description: The concentration of the CO2 in the reference cylinder used in the field calibration
GRP_EC.explanation: Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS and with EC_TYPE "Field Calibration" or "Field Calibration Check". This variable can be submitted only together with EC_GA_CAL_OFFSET.

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_CAL_H2O_ZERO
GRP_EC.description: The zero H2O reading using reference dry cylinder in the field calibration operation
GRP_EC.explanation: These are the readings prior to any change in the H2O zero settings. Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS and with EC_TYPE "Field Calibration" or "Field Calibration Check"

GRP_EC.name: EC_GA_CAL_TA
GRP_EC.description: Ambient air temperature where and when the gas analyser was calibrated
GRP_EC.explanation: In case the field calibration happens in a hut report the internal temperature of the hut. Can be reported only if EC_MODEL is either GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200 or GA_CP-LI-COR LI-7200RS and with EC_TYPE "Field Calibration" or "Field Calibration Check"

GRP_EC.name: EC_LOGGER
GRP_EC.description: ID of the Logger where variable is registered (the LN value used in the file name)
GRP_EC.explanation: Report here the ID number logger (specified in the LOGGER group) where the measurements made by the instrument are registered. The file name requires two digits but in this variable report only the integer value (e.g. for "L03" in filename report 3). This variable can be reported only together with the EC_SAMPLING_INT and EC_FILE and with EC_TYPE either "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_FILE
GRP_EC.description: ID of the File where variable is registered (the FN value used in the file name)
GRP_EC.explanation: Report here the ID number of the file (specified in the FILE group) where the measurements made by the instrument are registered. The file name requires two digits but in this variable report only the integer value (e.g. for "F03" in filename report 3). This variable can be reported only together with the EC_SAMPLING_INT and EC_LOGGER and with EC_TYPE either "Installation" or "Maintenance"

GRP_EC.name: EC_DATE
GRP_EC.description: Instrument operations, maintenance or event date
GRP_EC.explanation: Date of validity of the GRP_EC information provided. This is one of the alternatives, the other is DATE_START and DATE_END. It is the only possibility when EC_TYPE is Installation or Removal or Maintenance together + another optional variable

GRP_EC.name: EC_DATE_START

GRP_ECWEXCL.name: ECWEXCL
GRP_ECWEXCL.description: Centre of the wind sector to be excluded in the EC data analysis
GRP_ECWEXCL.explanation: Report the centre of the wind sector that should be excluded in the eddy covariance data processing. It is not needed to report the wind sector behind the sonic if it is +/- 10 degrees because it is automatically considered in the processing. If instead you propose to exclude more (large tower, different landuse etc.) please report it. When this group is submitted all the variables are mandatory except the COMMENT.

GRP_ECWEXCL.name: ECWEXCL_RANGE
GRP_ECWEXCL.description: Size of the wind sector to be excluded in the EC data analysis
GRP_ECWEXCL.explanation: Report the size of the wind sector that should be excluded in the eddy covariance data processing. For example in case the sector is between 60 and 100 degrees N, this variable will have value 40 (100-60) and ECWEXCL will be 80. It is not needed to report the wind sector behind the sonic if it is +/- 10 degrees because it is automatically considered in the processing. When this group is submitted all the variables are mandatory except the COMMENT. The variable if submitted must be >1.

GRP_ECWEXCL.name: ECWEXCL_NORTHREF

Angles or distances respect to True North (corrected for the magnetic declination)

GRP_ECWEXCL.name: ECWEXCL_ACTION

GRP_ECWEXCL.explanation: Use this variable to report if the wind sector is added or removed. In case of removal (e.g. because the footprint situation changed and the sector can be used or because you need to replace it with a larger sector) you need to report exactly the same ECWEXCL and ECWEXCL_RANGE of the active sector and "Removing" as value. choices.description: Use this if the wind exclusion sector is added

GRP_ECWEXCL.name: ECWEXCL_COMMENT

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_SOIL
GRP_MNG.description: Soil management operation type
GRP_MNG.explanation: Select the type of soil management operation performed from the predefined list LIST(MNG_SOIL). Each distinct soil management event must be reported as a separate entry even if performed with the same machine passage. The different tools used, the type of machine and the duration of the machine operation can be reported using the group of MNG_MACHINE_* variables

choices.description: Burying. Incorporation of organic matter, crop residues, or amendments into the soil by covering them with a layer of earth, without necessarily inverting the soil profile.
Crushing stones. Mechanical fragmentation of stones on or near the soil surface to facilitate tillage, improve seedbed quality, or reduce implement damage.
Drainage. Installation or maintenance of drainage infrastructure (e.g. ditches, tile drains, mole drains) to remove excess water from the soil profile and reduce waterlogging.
Furrowing. Creation of narrow linear channels in the soil surface for seeding, irrigation water distribution, or drainage purposes.
Harrowing. Secondary tillage operation using tined or disc harrows to break up clods, level the soil surface, and incorporate crop residues or amendments after primary tillage.
Hilling. Mounding of soil around the base of crop plants to support stem stability, encourage adventitious rooting, or protect tubers from light exposure (e.g. potatoes).
Hoeing. Shallow manual or mechanical soil disturbance around crop plants to control weeds, break soil crust, and improve surface aeration.
Other oil management operation not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Removal of peat from the footprint area. Physical extraction of peat material from the tower footprint area, altering soil organic matter content, surface elevation, and hydrological properties.
Plowing. Primary tillage operation using a moldboard or disc plow to invert and break up the soil profile, burying surface residues and incorporating organic matter to depth.
Rewetting. Voluntary restoration of water levels in previously drained soils, particularly in peatlands or wetlands, to reverse drainage effects and restore hydrological conditions.
Ridging. Formation of raised soil ridges and furrows across the field, typically to improve drainage, facilitate hilling, or prepare beds for row crops.
Rolling. Compression of the soil surface using a roller to improve seed-to-soil contact, consolidate loose seedbeds, or flatten crop residues

Scarification. Mechanical disturbance of the soil surface and/or organic layer to expose mineral soil or loosen shallow compaction, typically used in forestry to prepare seedbeds for natural regeneration or planting, and in cropland/grassland to break soil crust and improve surface aeration.
Scratching. Shallow surface disturbance of the topsoil layer using light implements, used to break soil crust, incorporate surface amendments, or stimulate germination.

Screefing. A site preparation technique used in forest management that consists of manually or mechanically clearing away the surface layer of vegetation, organic debris, moss, litter, and duff from a small patch of soil in order to expose the underlying mineral soil beneath.
Soil compaction. Physical compression of soil structure resulting from mechanical pressure (e.g. machinery, trampling), reducing pore space.
Strip till. Conservation tillage practice where only narrow strips of soil (typically 20–30 cm wide) are tilled along the planting row, leaving inter-row soil undisturbed.
Subsoiling. Deep tillage operation penetrating below the normal plowing depth to break up compacted subsoil layers (hardpan), improving water infiltration and root penetration.
Conventional Tillage. Full soil inversion and disturbance across the entire field using multiple implements (e.g. plow, harrow, roller), disrupting soil structure to prepare a seedbed.
Turf-stripping. Physical removal of the surface turf layer, including vegetation and its associated root mat, typically for land preparation, peatland restoration, or ecosystem management purposes.
Under-vine plowing. Shallow tillage operation performed in the inter-row or under-vine strip of vineyards to control weeds and incorporate surface residues without disturbing vine roots.

GRP_MNG.description: Depth of the soil management operation
GRP_MNG.explanation:
Report the depth of the soil management operation in metres (m). Only report this variable when the depth is meaningful and relevant to the operation (e.g., tillage depth, drainage depth). Leave blank if the operation does not have a defined depth or if the information is not available.
When reported, also MNG_SOIL_DEPTH_STATISTIC must be reported.

Uncertainty may be reported from the instrument's specifications, determined empirically, or estimated by the tower team. Please describe such details in Approach. For uncertainty values that are better described by a range, a percent, or other, please enter information in Comments.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_SOIL_DEPTH_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_MNG.description: Depth of the soil management operation statistic method
GRP_MNG.explanation: Can be reported only if MNG_SOIL_DEPTH_STATISTIC is also reported

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_SOW
GRP_MNG.description: Plants sowing or planting operation type
GRP_MNG.explanation: Select the type of sowing or planting operation performed from the predefined list LIST(MNG_SOW). Each sowing or planting event must be reported as a separate entry.

choices.description: Cuttings. Vegetative propagation method where stem, leaf, or root fragments are placed into the soil or growing medium to develop into new individual plants.
Direct sowing. Sowing of seeds directly into undisturbed soil or standing crop residues without prior seedbed preparation, typically associated with no-till or conservation agriculture systems.
Other sowing or planting method not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.

Planting. Establishment of vegetation by placing seedlings, transplants, bulbs, tubers into the soil or growing material. In case of direct sowing with seeds use the other options in the LIST(MNG_SOW).
Precision sowing. Sowing method using precision seed drills to place individual seeds at exact spacing, depth, and intervals.
Surface sowing. Sowing of seeds into a previously prepared seedbed following primary and/or secondary tillage operations, using standard seed drill equipment at defined row spacing and depth.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_SOW_QUANTITY_UNIT

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_PLANT_ACTIVITY
GRP_MNG.description: Plant management operation type
GRP_MNG.explanation: Select the type of plant management operation performed from the predefined list LIST(MNG_PLANT). Each distinct event must be reported as a separate entry.

choices.description: Clearcutting. Silvicultural operation in which all trees within a defined stand or management unit are felled in a single intervention, regardless of species, size, or condition. After this the site is generally left for natural regeneration or replanted.
Complantation cutting back layering. A vine or orchard establishment technique combining planting with cutting back, layering or grafting to renew or fill gaps in a row.
Removal of contaminated organs. The targeted removal and disposal of plant organs (leaves, shoots, fruit) showing signs of disease, pest damage or chemical contamination.
Crop topping. A mechanical topping operation that removes the upper portion of the crop canopy to control height, improve uniformity or facilitate harvest.
Disbudding. A manual or mechanical operation that removes unwanted buds from shoots or canes to concentrate growth into selected positions.
Grubbing up. The complete removal of perennial crops, vines or trees including their root systems, typically to prepare the land for replanting or change of use.
Harvesting. A mechanical or manual collection of mature crop produce from the field, orchard or vineyard at the appropriate stage of ripeness.
Leaf stripping. A canopy management operation that removes leaves around the fruit zone to improve light exposure, air circulation and fruit quality.
Lifting. A canopy management operation that raises drooping foliage or fruiting canes and tucks them into the trellis wire system.
Manual weeding. Hand removal of unwanted vegetation from the soil surface or around crop plants.
Mechanical weeding. Removal of unwanted vegetation using mechanical implements (e.g. inter-row cultivators, brush weeders), without the use of herbicides.
Mowing. Cutting of grass, forage crops or cover crops at or near the soil surface for hay, silage or vegetation management purposes.
Other plant management or harvesting-related action not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Prescribed or controlled Fire. Deliberately ignited and managed fire, conducted under planned conditions to achieve specific land or ecosystem management objectives within defined boundaries.
Presize. A mechanical pre-pruning pass that reduces canopy volume before hand finishing, typically performed with a reciprocating cutter bar.
Pressing. The mechanical compression of mown forage or crop material into bales for storage, transport or ensiling.
Pruning. A dormant-season pruning operation that removes selected canes, branches or spurs to shape the plant and regulate the following season's yield.
Pruning in green. A summer pruning operation carried out on green, actively growing shoots to limit canopy size and improve fruit exposure and ripening.
Salvage Logging. A harvesting operation that removes timber damaged or killed by fire, storm, pest or disease to recover economic value and reduce hazard.
Shelterwood cutting. A silvicultural system in which mature trees are felled in successive stages to provide shelter for natural regeneration of the understorey.
Shredding. A mechanical operation that shreds, crushes or grinds vegetation into small pieces, whether it is tall grass, cover crops, brush, pruning, woody small branches, stubble or crop residue.
Silage. The harvesting and ensiling of fresh forage crops by chopping and compacting the material in a silo or clamp to produce fermented feed.
Suckering. A canopy management operation that removes unwanted lateral shoots (suckers) growing from the base or trunk of vines or trees.
Tarpaulin. Application of opaque plastic or fabric sheeting over the soil surface to suppress weed emergence through light exclusion and soil heating.
Tedding. A post-mowing operation that spreads and turns cut forage to improve aeration and accelerate field drying before baling.
Thermal weeding. Destruction of unwanted vegetation using heat application (e.g. flame weeding, steam, infrared radiation), without the use of chemicals or mechanical soil disturbance.
Thinning/Selective cutting. A selective silvicultural operation that removes a proportion of trees from a stand to improve light, space and resources for the remaining trees.
Trellising. The installation or maintenance of a support structure of posts and wires to train and guide crop growth along defined rows.
Tying attachment folding. A manual or mechanical operation that attaches canes, shoots or branches to a support structure by tying, clipping or folding.
Windrowing. A harvest-related operation that rakes or sweeps cut material into parallel rows (windrows) to facilitate collection, drying or baling.

choices.description: Exported AGB Biomass: all the aboveground biomass
Exported branches. Woody lateral branches removed from trees or shrubs. Only woody vegetation.
Exported fruit. Fleshy or dry fruits and reproductive structures harvested and removed (including flowers).
Exported grain. Cereal or pulse grain removed from the field after harvest.
Other plant material export activity not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Exported residues. Residues exported also after a defined period spent in the field. Could follow a period of residues left on field (Residue Left).
Exported stem. Above-ground stem biomass removed from cropland or grassland.
Exported Straw. Cereal stem and leaf residues removed after grain harvest.
Exported trunks: Main woody stem of felled trees removed as timber or biomass. Only woody vegetation.
Exported tuber. Underground storage organs (e.g. roots and tubers) harvested and removed from the field.
Residue buried and incorporated into the soil by tillage after harvest.
Residue burned in field after harvesting.
Residue left intact on the field surface after harvest.

Residue mechanically shredded and left on the field surface after harvest.

GRP_MNG.explanation: Select the method used to determine the carbon content of the harvested material from the predefined list LIST(MNG_HARVESTED_MAT_CN_METHOD). This variable can be reported only when MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_C_CONTENT is submitted.

choices.description: C and N content measured by dry combustion using a CHNS elemental analyser on a representative sample of the harvested material.
N content determined by high-temperature combustion with thermal conductivity detection. Can be used only with the MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_N_CONTENT_METHOD variable.

N content determined by wet acid digestion followed by steam distillation and titration; measures total Kjeldahl nitrogen (organic N + ammonium). Can be used only with the MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_N_CONTENT_METHOD variable.

C content determined by Loss-on-Ignition (LOI). Organic matter content estimated by weight loss after combustion at 400–550°C; C content derived indirectly using a conversion factor. Can be used only with the MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_C_CONTENT_METHOD variable.
C and N content estimated by mid-infrared (MIR) spectroscopy.
C and N export estimated using a process-based or empirical model; specify the model name and version in MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_COMMENT.
C and N content estimated by near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy (NIRS).
Other measurement method not in the list. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_COMMENT.
C and N content estimated by applying fixed C:N ratios (Stoichiometry Estimation) from published literature to the reported dry matter quantity.
C content determined by wet oxidation (Walkley-Black) with potassium or sodium dichromate. Can be used only with the MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_C_CONTENT_METHOD variable.
C or N export calculated by multiplying the harvested yield by published conversion coefficients (Yield Coefficient) specific to the crop type and component.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_N_CONTENT_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_MNG.description: Percentage of nitrogen in the dry matter of the harvested component method
GRP_MNG.explanation: Can be reported only if MNG_HARVESTED_MATERIAL_N_CONTENT_STATISTIC is also reported

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_GRAZE_TYPE
GRP_MNG.description: Type of grazing activity
GRP_MNG.explanation: Use the predefined list in LIST(MNG_GRAZE_TYPE) to report how grazing was conducted in terms of spatial and temporal patterns.

choices.description: It is a sub-category of continuous grazing where stocking pressure is continuously adjusted throughout the season based on observed forage availability.
Grazing management where livestock have unrestricted access to the entire pasture area within the eddy covariance tower footprint throughout the grazing season, with no rotation or rest periods.
Grazing management where part of the vegetation is periodically cut and the remaining biomass is subsequently grazed by livestock within the tower footprint.
Combination of two or more grazing management strategies applied within the eddy covariance tower footprint during the year.

High-intensity rotational grazing using a large number of paddocks within the tower footprint, characterized by very short grazing periods (hours to 1–2 days) and long recovery intervals to optimize forage regrowth. Distinguished from Rotational by the high paddock number and precision of recovery management.

Grazing management where livestock are moved between a small number of paddocks within the tower footprint, with moderate grazing periods (days to weeks) and scheduled rest intervals to allow forage recovery.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_GRAZE_BIOMASS_METHOD

GRP_MNG.explanation: Report the method used to quantify the biomass removed by grazing using one of the predefined options in the LIST(MNG_GRAZE_BIOMASS_METHOD)

choices.description: Animal intake estimation. Consumed biomass back-calculated from animal intake estimates based on live weight, production level, and nutritional requirements.
Exclusion cage. Biomass consumption estimated by comparing vegetation growth inside paired exclusion cages (no grazing) versus grazed plots over a defined period.
Cut and weigh. Vegetation biomass measured by cutting and weighing samples before and after a grazing period within a defined area.
Faecal marker method.  Consumption estimated using indigestible external markers (e.g. chromium, alkanes) to quantify individual animal dry matter intake.
Consumed biomass estimated using a process-based or empirical model from animal and sward input data.
Other grazed biomass estimation method not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Remote sensing. Biomass consumption estimated from vegetation indices (e.g. NDVI) derived from satellite, drone, or aerial imagery before and after grazing.

Rising Plate Meter (RPM). Sward height measured with a rising plate meter before and after grazing; converted to biomass using a site-specific calibration equation. The equation used can be added in the  MNG_COMMENT variable.
Sward height measurement. Biomass estimated from sward height measured with a ruler or graduated stick, converted to dry matter using a site-specific height-to-biomass calibration equation.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_IRRIGATION
GRP_MNG.description: Irrigation activity reported
GRP_MNG.explanation: Select the irrigation operation to be reported using the list LIST(MNG_IRRIG)

choices.description: Irrigation through furrows opened between crop rows. Details regarding furrow depth, spacing, orientation relative to slope, and run length can be provided in MNG_COMMENT.
Underground irrigation system delivering water at depth directly to the root zone via buried emitters. Typically used in perennial crops (trees, vines).
Low-pressure micro-sprinklers or diffusers delivering fine spray over a small area around each plant. Typically used in orchards and vineyards.

Porous or micro-perforated tubes buried or laid on the surface that release water by seepage or micro-droplets directly into the root zone. Typically suited in vegetable crops, strawberries, and vines.
Other irrigation methods not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Center pivot sprinkler lateral anchored at its centre and rotating in a circle around the water supply point. Typically used in arable crops (maize, alfalfa, potato).
Sprinkler network of lateral pipes manually relocated by the operator between positions after each irrigation cycle.
Self-propelled sprinkler lateral moving in continuous linear translation across the field. Typically used in large rectangular arable fields (wheat, maize, sugar beet).
Perforated pipes laid on the ground or elevated, delivering water as fine rain. Typically used temporarily and then relocated in market gardening, nurseries, and greenhouse crops.
Network of fixed sprinklers permanently installed throughout the field, often with continuous or scheduled operation. Typically used in orchards, vineyards.
High-pressure sprinkler that delivers water in a wide rotary jet, covering large areas from a single fixed or wheeled position.
Sprinkler lateral mounted on large wheels that are mechanically rolled from one position to the next. Typically used in large rectangular fields of cereals or fodder crops.
Network of buried drains that simultaneously manage excess water removal and water supply through capillary rise or controlled pressure. Typically used in meadows and wet arable land.

Irrigation through elongated strips or borders delimited by parallel earthen ridges. Water advances as a sheet from the upstream end to the downstream end. Typically used in meadows, cereals, and fodder crops.
Irrigation through rectangular compartments delimited by small earthen bunds. Water fills each cell uniformly. Typically used in rice paddies, meadows, and flat cropland.
Irrigation by uncontrolled submersion of the field; water is released and spreads freely without flow management. Typically used in rice cultivation and for soil leaching.
Irrigation through individual circular hollows dug around each tree or plant base. Water is retained locally. Typically used in fruit orchards and viticulture.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_IRRIGATION_PRECIP_MEAS
GRP_MNG.description: If the irrigation is measured by the rain gauge(s) installed at the station to measure precipitation, report the precipitation variable affected (in the form P_x_y_z)

If more than one rain variables are affected list them separated by comma (e.g. "P_1_1_1,P_1_1_2" reports that both the precipitation measurements are also affected by the irrigation)

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_PRODUCT_CATEGORY
GRP_MNG.description: Category of product applied to the site for fertilization, disease / pest control (phytosanitary products), or soil management.
GRP_MNG.explanation: Report the category of product applied to the site using the predefined list LIST(MNG_PRODUCT_CATEGORY)

choices.description: Liming. Application of calcium or magnesium-based materials (e.g. calcitic lime, dolomite, wood ash) to correct soil acidity, raise pH, and improve nutrient availability and soil structure.
Mineral Fertilizer. Synthetic or mined inorganic product applied to the soil or vegetation to supply one or more essential nutrients (e.g. N, P, K, S) in mineral form to support plant growth.
Organic Fertilizer. Product of biological origin applied to the soil to supply nutrients and improve soil organic matter content, including manure, compost, digestate, slurry, and crop residues.

Phytosanitary. Any chemical or biological product applied to vegetation or soil to prevent, control, or eliminate pests, diseases, or weeds, including herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, and nematicides.

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_PRODUCT_QUANTITY_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_MNG.description: Quantity of the product distributed statistic method
GRP_MNG.explanation: Can be reported only if MNG_PRODUCT_QUANTITY_STATISTIC is also reported

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).
Estimate made by expert familiar with site

GRP_MNG.name: MNG_MACHINE_TOOL
GRP_MNG.description: Type of tool used for the operation
GRP_MNG.explanation: Report the type of tool used during management operation using one of the options available in the LIST(MNG_MACH_TOOL). Use MNG_MACHINE_VEHICLE to report the type of vehicle used with the tool. In case of multiple tools on the same vehicle report all the tools with different entries and same MNG_DATE_START and MNG_DATE_END and then the vehicle only once, associated to one of the tools.

choices.description: Chainsaw. A tree tool that fells trees and cuts timber into logs
Chipping machine. A tree tool that reduces wood branches and trimmings to wood chips for energy or compost
Chisel. A tillage tool for deep loosening without inversion that shatters compaction and breaks hardpan at 20–65 cm depth with partial soil mixing.
Corn detasseling machine. A harvest and mowing tool that removes tassels from corn plants for hybrid seed production
Corn picker. A harvest and mowing tool that harvests corn ears from standing stalks, optionally shelling or collecting whole cobs
Cover crop. A tillage tool that incorporates cover crop biomass into the topsoil to prepare for the next cash crop at 10–20 cm depth with partial soil mixing.
Cracker. A tillage tool that breaks soil clods and surface crust after primary tillage for surface refinement at 3–8 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Crushing machine. A harvest and mowing tool that crushes and conditions mown forage to accelerate field drying
Decompactor. A tillage tool for subsoil decompaction that fractures dense layers with minimal surface disturbance at 35–100 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Defoliator. A harvest and mowing tool that removes leaves from crops like tobacco or sugar beet before harvest
Disk harrow. A tillage tool that cuts and chops residue while breaking clods in primary or secondary tillage, working at 8–20 cm depth with partial soil mixing.
Drainage Trencher. An other‑category tool that cuts narrow trenches for installing subsurface drainage pipes at 30–120 cm depth while leaving surrounding soil unmixed.
Electrical weeding machine. A weed‑control tool that kills weeds using high‑voltage electrical current without disturbing or mixing the soil and with no defined working depth.
Fertilizer burier. A tillage tool that places and buries solid or liquid fertilizer at a defined depth in the soil at 10–25 cm with partial soil mixing.
Flame weeding machine. A weed‑control tool that destroys weeds at the soil surface with a propane flame and thermal shock, leaving the soil unmixed and with no specified depth.
Grapple skidder. A tree tool that drags logs from the felling site to the roadside using a grapple attachment.
Harvester (non-forest). A harvest and mowing tool that cuts, threshes and separates grain or other non‑forest crops.
Mower. A harvest and mowing tool that cuts grass, forage or cover crops at or near the soil surface.
Mulcher. A tool that shreds vegetation, stumps and brushwood, leaving the material as mulch on the surface, working at 0–5 cm depth with no soil mixing below that layer.
Other tool used not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Planter. A seeding and planting tool that places seed at precise spacing and depth, often together with fertilizer in the furrow, working at 3–10 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Plough. A tillage tool for primary tillage that cuts, lifts and fully inverts the soil slice, burying residues at 15–35 cm depth with full inversion.
Prepruner. A harvest and mowing tool that mechanically pre‑prunes vines or orchards before manual finishing.
Ridger. A tillage tool that forms raised ridges or beds and opens furrows for seed or drainage, working at 10–25 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Roller. A tillage tool that consolidates and levels the seedbed while breaking surface clods at 0–3 cm depth with no soil inversion or mixing.
Rotary cultivator. A tillage tool with a power take-off driven rotor that tills and mixes the topsoil intensively for fine seedbed preparation at 10–25 cm depth with full soil mixing.
Round baler. A transport and baling tool that rolls forage into cylindrical bales that may remain in the field or be wrapped.
Seedbed cultivator. A tillage tool that refines the seedbed by breaking clods and levelling the surface before sowing, operating at 5–12 cm depth with partial soil mixing.
Seeder. A seeding and planting tool that broadcasts or drills seed at a uniform depth and rate across a seedbed, operating at 2–8 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Silage wagon. A transport and baling tool that collects and transports chopped forage from the harvester to the silo.
Spader. A tillage tool whose spading blades mimic hand digging to provide deep tillage without creating a compaction pan at 20–40 cm depth with full soil mixing.
Sprayer. An other‑category tool that applies liquid chemicals such as pesticides, herbicides or fertilizers to crops or soil, working with no soil mixing or specified depth.
Spreader. An other‑category tool that distributes solid amendments such as fertilizer, lime or manure over the soil surface, operating without soil mixing or defined depth.
Square baler. A transport and baling tool that compresses mown forage into rectangular bales for storage or transport.
Stone burier. A tillage tool that pushes surface stones below the soil surface to leave a clean seedbed, operating at 15–25 cm depth with full soil mixing.
Stubble cultivator. A tillage tool that incorporates post‑harvest stubble and residue in shallow secondary tillage at 8–15 cm depth with partial soil mixing.
Stump grinder. A tree tool that grinds tree stumps below ground level using a rotating cutting wheel, operating at 10–30 cm depth with no associated soil mixing classification.
Suckering machine. A harvest and mowing tool that removes lateral shoots or suckers from crops such as tobacco or vines.
Swather (windrower). A harvest and mowing tool that cuts the crop and lays it into windrows for field drying before baling or combining.
Plastic tarp decoiler. A weed‑control tool that lays plastic mulch film on beds to suppress weeds and retain soil moisture, acting at the surface with no soil mixing or depth specification.
Tedder. A harvest and mowing tool that spreads and aerates mown forage to speed curing and drying.

Tine harrow. A tillage tool to refine seed-bed conditions before planting, remove small weeds in growing crops, and loosen the inter-row soils to allow water to soak into the subsoil, working at 2-5 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Tipping-trailer. A transport and baling rear‑tipping trailer used for bulk transport of grain, soil, manure or compost.
Topping machine. A harvest and mowing tool that removes the tops of root crops such as sugar beet before harvest, with no soil mixing or specified depth.
Trailer. A transport and baling general‑purpose towed vehicle for moving goods in field and on road.
Weeder. A weed‑control tool that mechanically uproots or buries weeds by inter‑row or intra‑row cultivation at 2–8 cm depth with no soil mixing.
Winch-skidder. A tree tool that drags logs to the roadside using a winch cable.
Wood processor. A tree tool that delimbs and bucks felled trees into logs.
Wrapper. A transport and baling tool that wraps round bales in plastic film for anaerobic silage fermentation.

GRP_MNG.description: Type of vehicle used for the operation
GRP_MNG.explanation: Report the type of vehicle used during the management operation using one of the options available in the LIST(MNG_MACH_VEHIC). A vehicle can be associated with a specific tool from the list (MACH_TOOL). However, if the same vehicle is used to carry out different operations at the same time, the vehicle should be reported only once, associated to one of the tools used. choices.description: Cable yarder. A cable-based log extraction system that uses suspended lines to move felled timber from steep or sensitive terrain to a landing.
Combine-harvester. A self-propelled machine that cuts, threshes and cleans grain or other arable crops in a single pass.
Excavator-based harvester. An excavator chassis retrofitted with a forestry harvesting head, used for felling, delimbing, and bucking trees into logs.
Feller buncher. A self-propelled forestry machine that fells and accumulates multiple trees into bunches at the stump for subsequent extraction.
Forage harvester. A self-propelled or tractor-mounted machine that cuts, chops and collects forage crops such as grass or maize in a single pass.
Forest harvester. A self-propelled forestry machine equipped with a harvesting head that fells, delimbs and bucks trees into logs in a single pass.
Forklift . A powered industrial vehicle equipped with front forks used for lifting and moving palletised or heavy loads in farm yards and stores.
Forwarder. A self-propelled forestry vehicle with a load bunk and grapple that transports cut logs from the felling site to the roadside.
Grape harvesting machine. A self-propelled or tractor-mounted machine that harvests grape bunches from vine rows by shaking or stripping.
Helicopter. An aerial vehicle used for log extraction or agricultural operations in areas inaccessible to ground machinery.
Other self-propelled or towed vehicle not listed. Insert the details and explanation in the MNG_COMMENT.
Quad. A four-wheeled all-terrain vehicle used for light transport, field inspection and tool-carrying operations.
Self-propelled chipping machine. A self-propelled machine that processes whole trees or woody residues into wood chips directly in the field or at roadside.
Self-propelled forest carriage. A self-propelled forest carriage that runs along a cable skyline to transport logs from the felling area to the extraction road.
Tractor. A wheeled or tracked agricultural power unit used to pull, push or drive a wide range of mounted, semi-mounted or trailed implements.
Truck. A road vehicle used for transporting agricultural or forestry products, machinery and materials between farm, forest and market.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_TYPE
GRP_DISTURB.description: Type of disturbance
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Report the type of disturbance reported using one of the options available in LIST(DIST_TYPE). A disturbance is defined as an event not expected, non-voluntary and not controlled by humans. If the type of disturbance is not listed, use one of the Other options.

choices.description: Derecho (Abiotic Disturbance). Widespread, long-lived wind storm that is associated with a band of rapidly moving showers or thunderstorms.

Drought (Abiotic Disturbance). Prolonged period of abnormally low water availability, causing soil moisture deficit that stresses or damages vegetation through desiccation, reduced photosynthesis, and wilting.

Flood (Abiotic Disturbance). Temporary inundation of land by excess water resulting from intense precipitation, river overflow, snowmelt, or storm surge, exceeding the natural drainage capacity of the area.
Freeze (Abiotic Disturbance). Meteorological event in which air and/or soil temperatures drop below 0°C, causing ice formation in the surrounding environment for a significant duration.

Heatwave (Abiotic Disturbance). Prolonged period of abnormally high temperatures causing heat stress, accelerated water loss, protein denaturation, and impaired photosynthesis in affected vegetation. Heatwave is defined as extended period of excessively high air temperatures, significantly above seasonal norms.

Hurricane (Abiotic Disturbance). Tropical cyclone characterized by sustained high winds (≥119 km/h), heavy rainfall, and storm surge, generating extreme mechanical and hydrological forces across the affected area.

Insect (Biotic Disturbance). Outbreak or infestation of herbivorous or phytophagous insect species (e.g. defoliators, borers, sap-suckers) occurring at densities sufficient to cause measurable ecosystem disturbance.
Other Abiotic disturbance not in the list. Insert the details and explanation in the DISTURB_COMMENT.
Other Biotic disturbance not in the list. Insert the details and explanation in the DISTURB_COMMENT.

Pathogen (Biotic Disturbance). Introduction or proliferation of disease-causing microorganisms (fungi, bacteria, viruses, oomycetes) at levels sufficient to cause widespread infection across the affected ecosystem.
Sediments deposition (Abiotic Disturbance). Sediments deposited on the ground after a flood  or other transports of material.

Storm (Abiotic Disturbance). Intense short-duration meteorological event characterized by strong winds, hail, and/or heavy precipitation, generating significant mechanical and hydrological forces locally.
Tornado (Abiotic Disturbance). Violently rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm to the ground, with extremely high wind speeds causing intense localized destruction over a narrow path.
Uncontrolled Fire (Abiotic Disturbance).
Wild herbivory (Biotic Disturbance). Grazing, browsing, or trampling by wild animal populations at intensities exceeding the natural regeneration capacity of the ecosystem.

The rooting system
The whole plant
The whole aboveground part of the plant
The woody above ground part of the plant

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_AFFECTED_SEVERITY
GRP_DISTURB.description: Degree of severity of the disturbance event
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Knowing that it is a subjective evaluation, rate the level of impact expected using the options available in LIST(DIST_SEV) respect to the maximum possible for the type of disturbance

choices.description: High. Severe damage causing significant loss of biomass or function in the affected organ. Partial mortality possible; recovery is slow and may require management intervention.
Low. Slight damage observable on the affected organ. Minor physiological stress with limited effect on biomass or function. Full recovery expected within a short period.
Maximum. Complete or near-total destruction of the affected organ relative to the worst-case impact expected for this disturbance type. Recovery unlikely without active restoration.
Medium. Moderate damage to the affected organ with partial loss of function or biomass. Recovery is possible but may require time or favourable conditions.
Minimal. Negligible impact on the affected organ or vegetation. No structural damage; physiological functions fully maintained. Natural recovery expected without intervention.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_AFFECTED_QUANTITY
GRP_DISTURB.description: Quantity of organ biomass affected by the event
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Quantity of biomass of the organ specified in DISTURB_AFFECTED_ORGAN affected by the event expressed in kg of dry matter per m2. Can be submitted only if DISTURB_AFFECTED_ORGAN is reported. When reported, also DISTURB_AFFECTED_QUANTITY_STATISTIC must be reported.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_AFFECTED_QUANTITY_STATISTIC

GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Can be reported only if DISTURB_AFFECTED_QUANTITY is also reported

choices.description: Quantile at 10% of distribution
Quantile at 1% of distribution
Quantile at 25% of distribution
Quantile at 5% of distribution
Quantile at 75% of distribution
Quantile at 90% of distribution

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_AFFECTED_QUANTITY_STATISTIC_METHOD
GRP_DISTURB.description: Quantity of organ biomass affected statistic method
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Can be reported only if DISTURB_AFFECTED_QUANTITY_STATISTIC is also reported

choices.description: The statistic is aggregated from individual observations located within the site. Observations may be grouped into sample areas (e.g., plots) within the site but those groupings are ignored. Statistics generated from individual observations directly yield information on the site generally. The statistic may represent spatial characteristics of the measurement within the site (e.g., spatial heterogeneity) and/or characteristics due to other factors (e.g., population variability).

The statistic is aggregated from aggregated individual observations located in sample areas within the site. For example, individual observations are made in 5 sample plots within a site. "Aggregate of sample aggregates" is used if a plot statistic (e.g., Mean) is first calculated, and then the plot values are aggregated to calculate the site statistic. Statistics generated by this approach are often used to highlight the spatial characteristics within the site (i.e., the spatial heterogeneity of measurement within the site).

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION

GRP_DISTURB.explanation:

When submitted, also DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION_ANGLE and DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION_NORTHREF must be submitted.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION_ANGLE

Report the size of the wind sector affected by the disturbance event. For example in case the sector is between 60 and 100 degrees N, this variable will have value 40 (100-60) and DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION will be 80. The variable if submitted must be >1.
When submitted, also DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION and DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION_NORTHREF must be submitted.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION_NORTHREF

When submitted, also DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION and DISTURB_FETCH_DIRECTION_ANGLE must be submitted.

choices.description: Angles or distances respect to True North (corrected for the magnetic declination).
Angles or distances respect to Magnetic North.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_FETCH_FRACTION
GRP_DISTURB.description: Percentage of the target area affected by the disturbance event
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Report the % of the Target Area affected by the disturbance event.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_FETCH_MAP_FILENAME
GRP_DISTURB.description: Disturbed area map filename
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: If a map of the affected areas is available, report the filename of the map following the structure CC-sss_DISTURB_##########_YYYYMMDD.zzz, where CC-sss is the official station code, ########## are free text characters, YYYYMMDD is the DISTURB_DATE or DISTURB_START_DATE and zzz the file extension that can be kml or jpg. The map is uploaded separately

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_DATE
GRP_DISTURB.description: Date of the disturbance event
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Report the date of the disturbance event when a period can not be reported. Use DISTURB_DATE_UNC to report uncertainty in the date if needed. Can not be submitted if DISTURB_DATE_START and DISTURB_DATE_END are reported. Date should be truncated at the known resolution (e.g. if you know the starting minute of the disturbance use YYYYMMDDHHMM, if you only know the day use YYYYMMDD).

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_DATE_START

When submitted, also DISTURB_DATE_END must be submitted while DISTURB_DATE can not be reported.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_DATE_END
GRP_DISTURB.description: End date of the disturbance event
GRP_DISTURB.explanation: Report the ending date of the disturbance event reported. Date should be truncated at the known resolution (e.g. if you know the starting minute of the disturbance use YYYYMMDDHHMM, if you only know the day use YYYYMMDD). When submitted, also DISTURB_DATE_START must be submitted while DISTURB_DATE can not be reported.

GRP_DISTURB.name: DISTURB_DATE_UNC
GRP_DISTURB.description: Uncertainty in the date
